children.title: Multi-Step Ascent Methods
children.top_down_role: Descent–ascent methods using repeated maximizing-block updates per outer cycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Step Ascent Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One descent update followed by several inner ascent updates against a frozen primal variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For differentiable \(L(x,y)\), choose outer descent steps \(\alpha_k>0\), inner ascent steps \(\beta_{k,j}>0\), and integers \(q_k\geq1\). Initialize \((x^0,y^0)\). At outer iteration \(k\), set \(y^{k,0}=y^k\), compute
\[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k\nabla_xL(x^k,y^k),\]
and, with \(x^{k+1}\) held fixed, perform
\[y^{k,j+1}=y^{k,j}+\beta_{k,j}\nabla_yL(x^{k+1},y^{k,j}),\quad j=0,\ldots,q_k-1.\]
Set \(y^{k+1}=y^{k,q_k}\). Stop at a prescribed outer residual tolerance or iteration limit and return \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each descent step, hold the new minimizing variable fixed and perform one or more ascent steps on the maximizing variable.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is differentiable on the iterates' domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}\) is obtained after \(q_k\) ascent steps with \(x^{k+1}\) frozen.

notation.meaning: Number of inner ascent steps at outer iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The descent-first multi-step ascent algorithm is coherent, but no authoritative source or explicit domains for x and y are supplied.

children.title: Time-Scale Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relative-speed regimes governing tracking between minimizing and maximizing variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Scale Separation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-size and inner-loop predicates distinguishing comparable, ascent-fast, and idealized equilibrated-ascent regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\beta_k>0\) be descent and ascent step sizes, and define \(r_k=\beta_k/\alpha_k\). The scales are comparable when
\[0<\liminf_{k\to\infty}r_k\leq\limsup_{k\to\infty}r_k<\infty,\]
and ascent-fast when \(r_k\to\infty\). For an outer method using \(q_k\) inner ascent steps and producing \(y^{k+1}\), the idealized equilibrated-ascent regime is expressed by
\[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(y^{k+1},Y^*(x^{k+1})\bigr)\to0,\qquad Y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y}L(x,y).\]
These predicates classify scheduling; they do not by themselves imply convergence of the coupled iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Step-size ratios distinguish comparable and ascent-fast dynamics; vanishing distance to the current best-response set defines idealized equilibrated inner ascent.
assumptions_latex: The best-response set \(Y^*(x^{k+1})\) is nonempty whenever the equilibrated regime is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Comparable scales have bounded positive \(r_k\); ascent-fast scales have \(r_k\to\infty\); equilibrated ascent has distance to \(Y^*(x^{k+1})\) tending to zero.

notation.meaning: Maximizer or best-response set at fixed x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio predicates are coherent and condition fits the leaf, but the classification lacks a citation and the space and metric underlying the distance to the best-response set are unspecified.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Gradient Descent–Ascent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous gradient descent–ascent applied to a quadratically regularized saddle objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and choose \(\mu_x,\mu_y\geq0\). Define
\[L_{\mu}(x,y)=L(x,y)+\frac{\mu_x}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2-\frac{\mu_y}{2}\lVert y\rVert^2.\]
Given \((x^0,y^0)\) and \(\alpha_k,\beta_k>0\), regularized gradient descent–ascent performs
\[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k\bigl(\nabla_xL(x^k,y^k)+\mu_xx^k\bigr),\]
\[y^{k+1}=y^k+\beta_k\bigl(\nabla_yL(x^k,y^k)-\mu_yy^k\bigr).\]
Stop when the regularized gradient residual meets a prescribed tolerance, and return the latest pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply descent–ascent after adding quadratic convexity in the minimizing variable and quadratic concavity in the maximizing variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is gradient descent–ascent on \(L_\mu=L+(\mu_x/2)\lVert x\rVert^2-(\mu_y/2)\lVert y\rVert^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed iteration is correctly obtained from the quadratically regularized saddle objective, and algorithm fits the topic, but no authoritative citation supports this selected regularization variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Arrow–Hurwicz Dynamics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected continuous-time primal–dual dynamics for differentiable inequality-constrained convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). The Arrow–Hurwicz projected dynamics are
\[\dot x\in-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda)-N_X(x),\qquad \dot\lambda=\Pi_{T_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda)}g(x).\]
Equivalently, componentwise, \(\dot\lambda_i=g_i(x)\) when \(\lambda_i>0\), and \(\dot\lambda_i=\max\{g_i(x),0\}\) when \(\lambda_i=0\). An equilibrium satisfies primal stationarity together with dual feasibility, complementary slackness, and primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal variable follows projected Lagrangian descent while nonnegative multipliers follow projected constraint-violation ascent.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) and every component of \(g\) are differentiable.
Solutions are interpreted as projected differential-inclusion trajectories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every equilibrium satisfies \(0\in\nabla f(x)+Dg(x)^\mathsf T\lambda+N_X(x)\), \(g(x)\leq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Normal cone to X at x.
Tangent cone to the nonnegative orthant at lambda.
Euclidean projection onto tangent cone T.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equilibrium conditions are consistent with the displayed dynamics, but the continuous-time projected Arrow–Hurwicz variant and its differential-inclusion formulation require an authoritative source.

children.title: Uzawa Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical primal–dual schemes organized around primal subproblem resolution and multiplier evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Uzawa Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-primal-solve Uzawa iteration for convex programs with affine equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,Ax-b\rangle\). Given \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^m\) and step sizes \(\rho_k>0\), the exact Uzawa iteration computes
\[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\mathcal L(x,\lambda^k),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b).\]
Stop when both the feasibility residual \(\lVert Ax^{k+1}-b\rVert\) and an appropriate primal optimality residual meet prescribed tolerances, and return \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\). The multiplier update is gradient ascent on the differentiable dual function whenever the primal minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly minimize the Lagrangian over the primal variable, then ascend in the multiplier using the resulting equality-constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each displayed primal argmin is nonempty.
Dual differentiability is asserted only when the primal minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) solves the current Lagrangian subproblem and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-primal equality-constrained Uzawa iteration is coherent and algorithm is the correct kind, but it lacks a citation; the stated sufficient conditions for dual differentiability also require authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Given \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) and stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), compute
\[
x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda^k),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{R}_+^m}\bigl(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g(x^k)\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, \(g(x^k)\in\partial^+ d(\lambda^k)\) for the concave dual function \(d(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\), where \(\partial^+d\) denotes the concave superdifferential. Stop when a prescribed dual-gap, feasibility, or iteration criterion is met, and output the selected primal-dual iterate or an ergodic primal average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly minimize the Lagrangian in the primal variable, then take a projected supergradient-ascent step on the nonnegative dual multipliers.

children.title: Primal-Solve Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Exact and approximate primal-resolution regimes within dual-oriented dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Solve Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, summably inexact, and vanishing-error primal-oracle regimes for dual ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), an inexact primal oracle returns \(x^k\in X\) satisfying
\[
L(x^k,\lambda^k)\le d(\lambda^k)+\varepsilon_k,
\qquad d(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda),
\]
where \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\). The exact regime is \(\varepsilon_k=0\). A summably weighted inexact regime satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\). A vanishing-error regime satisfies \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), while a fixed-accuracy regime satisfies \(\varepsilon_k\le\bar\varepsilon\) and ordinarily supports convergence only to an error neighborhood. The applicable regime must be paired with the stepsize and convergence theorem used for the dual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal solves may be exact, summably inexact, asymptotically exact, or uniformly approximate; the error regime determines whether exact convergence or only neighborhood convergence is supportable.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\) is feasible for the primal domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-oracle regime is classified by \(\varepsilon_k=0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), or \(\sup_k\varepsilon_k\le\bar\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Mirror Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobi-style mirror descent for a differentiable convex-concave saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be closed convex sets, and let \(\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\). Let \(h_X\) and \(h_Y\) be differentiable strongly convex distance generators. From \((x^0,y^0)\in X\times Y\), simultaneously compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha_k\langle\nabla_x\Phi(x^k,y^k),x\rangle+D_{h_X}(x,x^k)\right\},
\]
\[
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}\left\{-\alpha_k\langle\nabla_y\Phi(x^k,y^k),y\rangle+D_{h_Y}(y,y^k)\right\}.
\]
Both gradients are evaluated at the same old iterate. Stop by a prescribed saddle-gap or iteration criterion and output a selected iterate or weighted ergodic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizing player takes a mirror step along its gradient, while the maximizing player simultaneously takes a mirror step against its negative gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty closed convex subsets of finite-dimensional normed spaces.
\(\Phi\) is differentiable, convex-concave, and finite on \(X\times Y\).
\(h_X\) and \(h_Y\) are differentiable and strongly convex on their domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed updates define simultaneous mirror descent-ascent for \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y)\).

children.title: Dual Averaging
children.top_down_role: Mirror-based dynamics driven by accumulated dual-space information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized dual averaging for a convex-concave saddle operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z=X\times Y\), let \(F(x,y)=(\nabla_x\Phi(x,y),-\nabla_y\Phi(x,y))\), and let \(h:Z\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be strongly convex. Initialize \(z^0\in Z\), \(s^0=0\), and choose weights \(\alpha_k>0\) and regularization scales \(\beta_k>0\). For \(k\ge0\), set
\[
s^{k+1}=s^k+\alpha_kF(z^k),\qquad
z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}\left\{\langle s^{k+1},z\rangle+\beta_{k+1}h(z)\right\}.
\]
Stop using a prescribed variational-inequality gap or iteration budget; a standard reported point is \(\bar z^N=(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulate all past saddle gradients in dual space, then recover each primal-dual iterate through a strongly convex regularized minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(Z=X\times Y\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The regularized minimization has a solution for every accumulated vector \(s^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}\) is the regularized dual-averaging response to \(\sum_{i=0}^{k}\alpha_iF(z^i)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\Delta_n\), \(Y=\Delta_m\), and let \(\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\). Initialize strictly positive \(x^0\in\Delta_n\) and \(y^0\in\Delta_m\). For \(\eta_k>0\), compute simultaneously
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k\exp(-\eta_k[\nabla_x\Phi(x^k,y^k)]_i)}{\sum_{r=1}^n x_r^k\exp(-\eta_k[\nabla_x\Phi(x^k,y^k)]_r)},
\]
\[
y_j^{k+1}=\frac{y_j^k\exp(\eta_k[\nabla_y\Phi(x^k,y^k)]_j)}{\sum_{s=1}^m y_s^k\exp(\eta_k[\nabla_y\Phi(x^k,y^k)]_s)}.
\]
Stop by a prescribed saddle-gap or iteration budget and output the chosen iterate or a weighted ergodic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each player exponentially reweights its simplex coordinates, decreasing the minimizer's costly coordinates and increasing the maximizer's rewarding coordinates, then normalizes.

children.title: Entropic Geometry Interface
children.top_down_role: Geometric correspondence linking multiplicative weighting to entropy-based mirror structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Geometry Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between simplex mirror steps and normalized exponential reweighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the probability simplex \(\Delta_n\), let \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). For \(x^k\in\operatorname{ri}(\Delta_n)\), \(g^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\eta_k>0\), the entropic mirror step
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Delta_n}\left\{\eta_k\langle g^k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x^k)\right\}
\]
has the coordinate representation
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k\exp(-\eta_k g_i^k)}{\sum_{j=1}^n x_j^k\exp(-\eta_k g_j^k)},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Thus the negative-entropy mirror map provides the exact interface between Bregman-proximal geometry and multiplicative weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-entropy mirror step on the simplex is exactly a normalized exponential, or multiplicative-weights, update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Mirror}_{h}(x^k,\eta_kg^k)_i=x_i^k e^{-\eta_kg_i^k}/\sum_jx_j^k e^{-\eta_kg_j^k}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Korpelevich's two-projection method for a monotone Lipschitz variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and seek \(z^\star\in C\) such that \(\langle F(z^\star),z-z^\star\rangle\ge0\) for every \(z\in C\). Given \(z^0\in C\) and \(0<\gamma<1/L\), iterate
\[
y^k=\Pi_C\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(z^k)\bigr),\qquad
z^{k+1}=\Pi_C\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(y^k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when a prescribed residual, gap, or iteration criterion is met, and output the selected last iterate or an ergodic average. The predictor \(y^k\) supplies the corrected operator evaluation used in the second projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient first predicts by a projected forward step, then corrects from the old point using the operator evaluated at the predictor.
assumptions_latex: The solution set of the variational inequality is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k=\Pi_C(z^k-\gamma F(z^k))\) and \(z^{k+1}=\Pi_C(z^k-\gamma F(y^k))\) define Euclidean extragradient.

children.title: Subgradient Extragradient

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One feasible projection followed by a projection onto its supporting halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(z^k\in C\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), form
\[
y^k=\Pi_C\bigl(z^k-\gamma_kF(z^k)\bigr),
\]
and define the supporting halfspace
\[
T_k=\left\{w\in\mathbb{R}^d:\left\langle z^k-\gamma_kF(z^k)-y^k,w-y^k\right\rangle\le0\right\}.
\]
Then set
\[
z^{k+1}=\Pi_{T_k}\bigl(z^k-\gamma_kF(y^k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when a prescribed variational-inequality residual or iteration criterion is met. The second projection is explicit because \(T_k\) is a halfspace, while \(C\subseteq T_k\) follows from the projection optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the predictor onto the feasible set, build its supporting halfspace, and replace extragradient's second feasible-set projection by a halfspace projection.
assumptions_latex: \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is defined at every generated predictor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=\Pi_{T_k}(z^k-\gamma_kF(y^k))\) is the subgradient-extragradient correction and \(C\subseteq T_k\).

notation.meaning: supporting halfspace containing the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a recognizable subgradient-extragradient update, and its algorithm kind fits the terminal, but it has no citation. Because named variants differ in their predictor, halfspace, stepsize, and convergence assumptions, an authoritative algorithm-level locator is required.

children.title: Hyperplane Extragradient
children.top_down_role: Extragradient variants using separating hyperplanes or halfspace corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperplane Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extragradient correction through a separating hyperplane generated by a trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(z^k\in C\), and choose a trial point \(y^k\in C\) satisfying \(\langle F(y^k),z^k-y^k\rangle>0\). Define
\[
H_k=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^d:\langle F(y^k),z-y^k\rangle=0\right\},
\qquad
T_k=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^d:\langle F(y^k),z-y^k\rangle\le0\right\}.
\]
Perform the corrected step
\[
z^{k+1}=\Pi_C\!\left(z^k-\rho_k\frac{\langle F(y^k),z^k-y^k\rangle}{\|F(y^k)\|^2}F(y^k)\right),\qquad 0<\rho_k<2.
\]
The unrelaxed inner displacement projects \(z^k\) onto \(H_k\); stop by a prescribed residual or iteration criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial operator value defines a separating hyperplane; the method projects toward that hyperplane and then restores feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correction direction is normal to \(H_k\), and its unrelaxed length equals the Euclidean distance from \(z^k\) to \(H_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and hyperplane-extragradient names cover multiple non-equivalent schemes. The stated positivity condition separates the current point from the displayed halfspace, but calling it a separating hyperplane for the variational-inequality solution set additionally requires operator and solution hypotheses that are not stated. A dedicated source is needed to determine the intended variant and orientation.

children.title: Subgradient-to-Hyperplane Connections
children.top_down_role: Structural links between subgradient evaluations and hyperplane-based corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-to-Hyperplane Connections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection residuals produce supporting hyperplanes used by subgradient-extragradient corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(u\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and set \(y=\Pi_C(u)\) and \(r=u-y\). Projection optimality gives
\[
\langle r,z-y\rangle\le0\quad\text{for every }z\in C.
\]
Hence
\[
C\subseteq T=\{z:\langle r,z-y\rangle\le0\},
\qquad H=\{z:\langle r,z-y\rangle=0\}
\]
is a supporting hyperplane when \(r\ne0\). In subgradient extragradient, taking \(u=z^k-\gamma_kF(z^k)\) converts the predictor projection residual into the halfspace or hyperplane used for the inexpensive corrective projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual of a feasible-set projection is a normal vector defining a containing halfspace and supporting hyperplane, linking subgradient and hyperplane extragradient constructions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u-y\in N_C(y)\), so \(C\subseteq\{z:\langle u-y,z-y\rangle\le0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking extragradient using a local predictor-corrector consistency test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, choose \(z^0\in C\), \(\bar\gamma>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\), choose the largest \(\gamma_k\in\{\bar\gamma\beta^j:j=0,1,\ldots\}\) such that, with \(y^k=\Pi_C(z^k-\gamma_kF(z^k))\),
\[
\gamma_k\|F(z^k)-F(y^k)\|\le\sigma\|z^k-y^k\|.
\]
Then update
\[
z^{k+1}=\Pi_C\bigl(z^k-\gamma_kF(y^k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when \(z^k=y^k\), a prescribed residual is small, or an iteration budget is reached; output the selected iterate or ergodic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack until the local operator variation is controlled by the predictor displacement, then perform the usual extragradient correction.
assumptions_latex: \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is continuous on the region containing generated points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted \(\gamma_k\) satisfies \(\gamma_k\|F(z^k)-F(y^k)\|\le\sigma\|z^k-y^k\|\) before the correction step.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Lipschitz Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracked extragradient for continuous monotone operators without a known global Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be continuous and monotone. Given \(z^k\in C\), select \(\gamma_k>0\) by backtracking until, for \(y^k=\Pi_C(z^k-\gamma_kF(z^k))\),
\[
\gamma_k\|F(z^k)-F(y^k)\|\le\sigma\|z^k-y^k\|,
\qquad \sigma\in(0,1).
\]
Set
\[
z^{k+1}=\Pi_C\bigl(z^k-\gamma_kF(y^k)\bigr).
\]
If \(y^k=z^k\), output \(z^k\); otherwise continue until a prescribed residual or iteration limit is reached. The acceptance test replaces any globally fixed restriction based on a Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous monotone operator lacking a usable global Lipschitz bound, backtracking enforces the local control needed by the extragradient correction.
assumptions_latex: The backtracking rule is well defined at every nonterminal iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method uses locally accepted steps satisfying \(\gamma_k\|F(z^k)-F(y^k)\|\le\sigma\|z^k-y^k\|\), without assuming a supplied global Lipschitz constant.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Acceptance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local backtracking test for Euclidean extragradient without a known global Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Euclidean space and let \(F:C\to\mathbb R^d\). Given \(x_k\in C\), a trial step \(\gamma>0\), and \(y=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(x_k))\), accept \(\gamma\) whenever \[\gamma\,\lVert F(y)-F(x_k)\rVert\leq \theta\,\lVert y-x_k\rVert,\qquad 0<\theta<1.\] If the test fails, replace \(\gamma\) by \(\beta\gamma\), where \(0<\beta<1\), and recompute \(y\). Under continuity of \(F\), the test is satisfiable for sufficiently small positive trial steps whenever \(y\neq x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a trial step when the local operator variation is dominated by the predictor displacement; otherwise shrink the step and recompute the predictor.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma\lVert F(y)-F(x_k)\rVert\leq\theta\lVert y-x_k\rVert\) is the acceptance boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Mirror-Prox
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-call deterministic Mirror-Prox for a monotone variational inequality in Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be closed and convex, let \(F:C\to E^*\), and let \(\omega\) be differentiable and strongly convex on \(C\). Define \(V_z(u)=\omega(u)-\omega(z)-\langle\nabla\omega(z),u-z\rangle\) and \(P_z(g)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\{\langle g,u\rangle+V_z(u)\}\). From \(z_1\in C\), perform \[w_t=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(z_t)),\qquad z_{t+1}=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(w_t)).\] After \(T\) iterations return \(\bar w_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\gamma_tw_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\gamma_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-Prox makes a Bregman predictor step, evaluates the operator there, performs a correction from the same base point, and averages predictors.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space.
\(\omega\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar w_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\gamma_tw_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\gamma_t)\) is the ergodic output.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Mirror-Prox
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-Prox for a monotone smooth operator plus a proximable convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:C\to E^*\) be monotone, let \(h:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define \(P_z(g)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\{\langle g,u\rangle+h(u)+V_z(u)\}\). Starting from \(z_1\in\operatorname{dom}h\), compute \[w_t=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(z_t)),\qquad z_{t+1}=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(w_t)).\] The associated composite variational inequality is to find \(z^\star\in C\) such that \(\langle F(z^\star),z-z^\star\rangle+h(z)-h(z^\star)\geq0\) for every \(z\in C\). Return a weighted average of \(w_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite Mirror-Prox incorporates the nonsmooth convex term into both Bregman proximal subproblems while evaluating only the smooth monotone operator.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable in the chosen geometry.
\(V_z\) is generated by a differentiable strongly convex function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_t=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(z_t))\) and \(z_{t+1}=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(w_t))\) define the composite iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Mirror-Prox
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking Mirror-Prox that estimates a valid local smoothness scale during execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(z_t\), choose a trial \(L_t>0\), set \(\gamma_t=L_t^{-1}\), and compute \(w_t=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(z_t))\) and \(z_{t+1}=P_{z_t}(\gamma_tF(w_t))\). Accept the trial when \[\gamma_t\langle F(w_t)-F(z_t),w_t-z_{t+1}\rangle\leq V_{z_t}(w_t)+V_{w_t}(z_{t+1}).\] Otherwise increase \(L_t\), recompute both proximal points, and retest. After the stopping criterion is reached, return the step-weighted average of accepted predictors. The test uses observed operator variation and does not require a supplied global Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive Mirror-Prox backtracks on a local smoothness estimate until the predictor-corrector error is controlled by the relevant Bregman divergences.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is monotone and locally Lipschitz on the iterates' domain.
The Bregman proximal mapping is well defined.
Rejected trials increase \(L_t\) by a factor greater than one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted steps satisfy \(\gamma_t\langle F(w_t)-F(z_t),w_t-z_{t+1}\rangle\leq V_{z_t}(w_t)+V_{w_t}(z_{t+1})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Popov Past-Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-new-call Euclidean past-extragradient iteration for a monotone variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Initialize \(x_0\in C\), choose \(y_{-1}\in C\), evaluate \(F(y_{-1})\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \[y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(y_{k-1})),\qquad x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(y_k)).\] Store \(F(y_k)\) for the next iteration. Thus, after initialization, each iteration introduces one new operator evaluation, at \(y_k\), while the predictor uses the stored past value. Return the final iterate or a prescribed average of \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Popov's method predicts with the previous auxiliary-point operator value and corrects with one newly evaluated value, requiring one new call per iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\gamma>0\) is chosen within the applicable convergence range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(y_{k-1}))\) and \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(y_k))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimistic Gradient Descent–Ascent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained OGDA written as an optimistic operator iteration for smooth convex-concave saddle problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable convex-concave function \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), define \(F(x,y)=(\nabla_xf(x,y),-\nabla_yf(x,y))\). For constrained domains, the displayed affine step must be replaced by a specified projected or proximal variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Reflected Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected reflected-point iteration for a monotone variational inequality in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(F:H\to H\). Given \(x_{-1},x_0\in C\) and \(\gamma>0\), form the reflected point \(r_k=2x_k-x_{k-1}\) and update
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k-\gamma F(r_k)\bigr),\qquad k\geq 0.
\]
Stop when a prescribed residual tolerance or iteration limit is reached, and return the latest iterate. Each iteration after initialization evaluates \(F\) once; the projection enforces \(x_{k+1}\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflect the current iterate across the previous one, evaluate the operator at that prediction, and project one forward step onto the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(C\subseteq H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(2x_k-x_{k-1}))\in C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Reflected Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-reflected-backward splitting using a reflected operator value and one new forward evaluation per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the inclusion \(0\in Ax+Bx\) on a real Hilbert space \(H\), choose \(x_{-1},x_0\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\). Initialize \(b_{-1}=Bx_{-1}\) and \(b_0=Bx_0\). For \(k\geq0\), compute
\[
x_{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x_k-\gamma(2b_k-b_{k-1})\bigr),
\qquad b_{k+1}=Bx_{k+1}.
\]
Stop at a chosen residual tolerance or iteration limit and return the latest iterate. Stored values make the iteration single-call in \(B\) after initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the backward resolvent after a forward step using twice the current operator value minus the previous value, requiring one new forward call per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}(x_k-\gamma(2Bx_k-Bx_{k-1}))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reflection Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar stability boundary for reflected-point gradient iteration on a monotone linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(H=C=\mathbb R\), \(F(x)=Lx\) with \(L>0\), and apply reflected-point gradient with constant stepsize \(\gamma>0\). Writing \(a=\gamma L\), the recurrence is
\[
x_{k+1}=(1-2a)x_k+a x_{k-1},
\]
with characteristic polynomial \(p(r)=r^2-(1-2a)r-a\). Both roots lie strictly inside the unit disk exactly when \(0<a<2/3\). At \(a=2/3\), one root equals \(-1\); for \(a>2/3\), some initial conditions produce nonconvergent or divergent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for the scalar monotone map F(x)=Lx, reflected-point gradient is stable exactly below γL=2/3; crossing the boundary produces an unstable characteristic root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization if and only if \(0<\gamma L<2/3\); unconditional convergence fails when \(\gamma L\geq2/3\).

notation.meaning: characteristic polynomial of the scalar recurrence

knowledge_statements.title: Tseng Forward–Backward–Forward
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tseng splitting for a maximally monotone plus monotone Lipschitz inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
To solve \(0\in Ax+Bx\) in a real Hilbert space \(H\), choose \(x_0\in H\) and stepsizes \(\gamma_k>0\). For \(k\geq0\), compute
\[
y_k=J_{\gamma_k A}(x_k-\gamma_k Bx_k),
\qquad
x_{k+1}=y_k-\gamma_k(By_k-Bx_k).
\]
Stop when a prescribed inclusion residual or iteration limit is reached and return the latest \(y_k\) or \(x_{k+1}\), according to the residual convention. The method uses one resolvent evaluation and two forward evaluations per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a forward-backward prediction, then correct it by the difference between the operator values at the prediction and current point.

children.title: Variable-Metric Forward–Backward–Forward

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Forward–Backward–Forward
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward–backward–forward splitting in a changing uniformly positive definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U_k:H\to H\) be self-adjoint and strongly positive. Given \(x_0\in H\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), perform
\[
y_k=J_{\gamma_k U_k^{-1}A}\bigl(x_k-\gamma_k U_k^{-1}Bx_k\bigr),
\qquad
x_{k+1}=y_k-\gamma_k U_k^{-1}(By_k-Bx_k).
\]
Stop at a prescribed residual tolerance or iteration limit and return the latest iterate. The metric changes both the resolvent and the two forward corrections; the constant-metric case \(U_k=I\) recovers Tseng forward–backward–forward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precondition each prediction and correction by a positive definite metric, allowing the geometry of forward–backward–forward splitting to vary with the iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) admits the displayed metric resolvents and \(B:H\to H\) is single-valued.
\(U_k\) is self-adjoint with \(U_k\succeq \alpha I\) for some \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=y_k-\gamma_kU_k^{-1}(By_k-Bx_k)\) with \(y_k=J_{\gamma_kU_k^{-1}A}(x_k-\gamma_kU_k^{-1}Bx_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Forward–Backward–Forward
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic FBF with conditionally unbiased estimates at both forward evaluation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be a filtration and let stochastic oracles return \(b_k\) at \(x_k\) and \(c_k\) at the resulting prediction. Starting from \(x_0\), set
\[
y_k=J_{\gamma_k A}(x_k-\gamma_k b_k),
\qquad
x_{k+1}=y_k-\gamma_k(c_k-b_k).
\]
Require \(\mathbb E[b_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=Bx_k\) and \(\mathbb E[c_k\mid\mathcal F_k,y_k]=By_k\). Stop at a prescribed stochastic-residual tolerance or iteration budget and return the latest iterate or a specified average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace both forward evaluations in FBF by conditionally unbiased oracle estimates while retaining the exact backward resolvent step.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) admits \(J_{\gamma_kA}\), and \(B:H\to H\) is single-valued.
The oracle estimates satisfy the displayed conditional unbiasedness relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k=J_{\gamma_kA}(x_k-\gamma_kb_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=y_k-\gamma_k(c_k-b_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Variable-Metric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard summable-variation and summable-noise regime for stochastic variable-metric splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be a filtration, let \(U_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable self-adjoint operators, and let \(e_k^x,e_k^y\) denote the two forward-oracle errors. A stochastic variable-metric regime is admissible when constants \(0<\alpha\leq\beta<\infty\) and a summable deterministic sequence \((\eta_k)\) exist such that
\[
\alpha I\preceq U_k\preceq\beta I,
\qquad U_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)U_k,
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k^2\mathbb E[\|e_k^x\|^2+\|e_k^y\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty
\]
almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metrics remain uniformly equivalent, their relative growth is summable, and stepsize-weighted conditional oracle variances have finite total mass.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\) and the oracle errors are adapted to \((\mathcal F_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha I\preceq U_k\preceq\beta I\), \(U_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)U_k\), and the displayed weighted conditional-error series is finite almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact resolvent iteration for finding a zero of a monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) and choose \(x_0\in H\) and \(\lambda_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the proximal inclusion exactly:
\[
0\in A x_{k+1}+\lambda_k^{-1}(x_{k+1}-x_k),
\]
equivalently,
\[
x_{k+1}=J_{\lambda_k A}x_k.
\]
Stop when a chosen inclusion or fixed-point residual is below tolerance, or when the iteration limit is reached, and return the latest iterate. Exactness means the displayed inclusion has no residual error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, exactly solve the regularized monotone inclusion, equivalently applying the operator resolvent to the current point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) has a well-defined resolvent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kA}x_k\), equivalently \(x_k-x_{k+1}\in\lambda_kAx_{k+1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-point iteration whose regularized inclusion is solved with a controlled residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), choose \(x_0\in H\), and let \(\lambda_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x_{k+1}\in H\), \(a_{k+1}\in Ax_{k+1}\), and an admissible residual \(e_{k+1}\in H\) satisfying
\[
x_k-x_{k+1}=\lambda_k a_{k+1}+e_{k+1}.
\]
The residual must obey the selected absolute or relative inexactness criterion. Stop at a prescribed outer residual tolerance or iteration limit and return the latest iterate. Setting \(e_{k+1}=0\) recovers exact proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve each proximal subproblem and retain an explicit residual that must satisfy a specified absolute or relative error rule.
assumptions_latex: Each residual \(e_{k+1}\) satisfies a declared inexactness criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k-x_{k+1}-e_{k+1}\in\lambda_kAx_{k+1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Inexactness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative residual criteria for an inexact proximal inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an inexact proximal step satisfies \(x_k-x_{k+1}=\lambda_k a_{k+1}+e_{k+1}\) with \(a_{k+1}\in Ax_{k+1}\). Two standard admissibility predicates are:
\[
\|e_{k+1}\|\leq\varepsilon_{k+1},
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_{k+1}<\infty,
\]
for summable absolute error, or
\[
\|e_{k+1}\|\leq\sigma\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,
\qquad 0\leq\sigma<1,
\]
for relative error. The chosen predicate is checked from the computed step and residual before accepting \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an approximate proximal step when its residual is bounded either by a summable absolute tolerance or by a fixed fraction of the step length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step is admissible if either \(\|e_{k+1}\|\leq\varepsilon_{k+1}\) with \(\sum_k\varepsilon_{k+1}<\infty\), or \(\|e_{k+1}\|\leq\sigma\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\) with \(\sigma<1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Proximal-Extragradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The relative-error HPE framework for a maximal monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
To solve \(0\in Tz\), choose \(z_0\in H\), \(0\leq\sigma<1\), and \(\lambda_k>0\). Select \((y_k,v_k,\varepsilon_k)\) satisfying
\[
v_k\in T^{[\varepsilon_k]}(y_k),
\qquad
\|\lambda_kv_k+y_k-z_{k-1}\|^2+2\lambda_k\varepsilon_k
\leq\sigma^2\|y_k-z_{k-1}\|^2,
\]
then update \(z_k=z_{k-1}-\lambda_kv_k\). Stop when \(\|v_k\|\) and \(\varepsilon_k\) meet prescribed tolerances, and return \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find an enlarged-operator evaluation satisfying a relative proximal error test, then take an extragradient-style update using that evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k=z_{k-1}-\lambda_kv_k\) for a triple satisfying the displayed HPE relative-error inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Proximal Minimax Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern-accelerated proximal-point template applied to the saddle operator of a convex–concave minimax problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be the monotone saddle operator associated with a convex–concave minimax problem, fix \(\lambda>0\), and choose an anchor \(z_0\in H\). For \(k\geq0\), compute the exact proximal point \(p_k=J_{\lambda T}z_k\) and set
\[
z_{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+2}z_0+\frac{k+1}{k+2}p_k.
\]
Stop when the fixed-point residual \(\|z_k-J_{\lambda T}z_k\|/\lambda\) is below tolerance or the iteration limit is reached; return \(p_k\). Inexact implementations must separately prescribe an inner-solve error schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply an anchored Halpern acceleration to the resolvent of the minimax saddle operator and monitor the normalized resolvent fixed-point residual.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) is a monotone saddle operator with single-valued resolvent.
Each displayed resolvent is evaluated exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient Iterative Regularization Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The simplest iterative-regularization variant for unconstrained minimization, performing one gradient step before changing the regularization parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Tikhonov Regularization for Variational Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional monotone VI with vanishing identity regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous and monotone. Suppose the solution set \(S=\{x\in C:\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\ \forall y\in C\}\) is nonempty. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the regularized variational inequality \[\langle F(x_\varepsilon)+\varepsilon x_\varepsilon,y-x_\varepsilon\rangle\geq0\qquad\forall y\in C\] has a unique solution. As \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), \(x_\varepsilon\) converges to the unique minimum-norm element \(P_S(0)\) of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive identity term makes the monotone VI uniquely solvable; as regularization vanishes, its solution approaches the minimum-norm original solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\to P_S(0)\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tikhonov Regularization Algorithm (TiRA)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing-regularization scheme in which each regularized VI is solved to a prescribed natural-residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\{\rho_k\}\downarrow0\), and \(\{\varepsilon_k\}\downarrow0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), stop if \(x^k\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\). Otherwise, compute \(x^{k+1}\) such that
\[
\bigl\|\mathbf F^{\mathrm{nat}}_{\varepsilon_k,K}(x^{k+1})\bigr\|\leq\rho_k,
\]
increment \(k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from any point and using residual tolerances and regularization parameters decreasing to zero, stop if the current iterate solves the original VI. Otherwise, choose the next point whose natural residual for the current regularized VI is at most the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\notin\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\Rightarrow\text{ choose }x^{k+1}\text{ satisfying }\bigl\|\mathbf F^{\mathrm{nat}}_{\varepsilon_k,K}(x^{k+1})\bigr\|\leq\rho_k.

children.title: Proximal Regularization
children.top_down_role: Proximal regularization routes for stabilizing VI or saddle subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent representation of a proximally regularized variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space, let \(F:C\to H\), and set \(T=F+N_C\). Given a center \(z\in H\) and \(\lambda>0\), proximal regularization seeks \(x_\lambda\in C\) satisfying \[0\in F(x_\lambda)+N_C(x_\lambda)+\lambda^{-1}(x_\lambda-z).\] Equivalently, \[x_\lambda=(I+\lambda T)^{-1}z=J_{\lambda T}z,\] or \(\langle F(x_\lambda)+\lambda^{-1}(x_\lambda-z),y-x_\lambda\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in C\). If \(T\) is maximal monotone, this point exists uniquely for every \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal regularization adds a quadratic pull toward a center; its solution is exactly the resolvent of the VI operator.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\lambda=J_{\lambda T}z\) is uniquely defined.

notation.meaning: resolvent of the scaled operator lambda T

children.title: Continuation Strategies
children.top_down_role: Stagewise variation of regularization or smoothing parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started continuation for a family of regularized monotone inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, fix \(z\in H\), choose \(\varepsilon_0>\varepsilon_1>\cdots>\varepsilon_K>0\), tolerances \(\eta_k\geq0\), and an initial point \(x^{-1}\). At stage \(k\), initialize the inner solver at \(x^{k-1}\) and compute \(x^k\) satisfying \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,T(x^k)+\varepsilon_k(x^k-z)\bigr)\leq\eta_k.\] Use \(x^k\) as the warm start for stage \(k+1\). Stop when \(k=K\), or when both the target regularization and residual tolerances are met, and return the final \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuation solves progressively less regularized inclusions, warm-starting each stage from the preceding approximate solution and controlling the stage residual.
assumptions_latex: Each inner stage can attain residual tolerance \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the last computed \(x^k\) satisfying the prescribed stage residual.

children.title: Continuation Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter-transition regimes governing stability across successive regularized problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniqueness and center stability when proximal regularization reaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone and define \(x_\varepsilon(z)\) by \(0\in T(x_\varepsilon)+\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon-z)\) for \(\varepsilon>0\). Then \(x_\varepsilon(z)=J_{T/\varepsilon}z\), so \[\|x_\varepsilon(z)-x_\varepsilon(w)\|\leq\|z-w\|.\] This uniform center stability need not extend to \(\varepsilon=0\), where uniqueness may disappear. Indeed, for \(T=0\), one has \(x_\varepsilon(z)=z\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), whereas the limiting inclusion \(0\in T(x)\) is satisfied by every \(x\in H\). Thus positive regularization is the boundary supporting unique continuation branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive proximal regularization gives a nonexpansive, unique branch; at zero regularization, uniqueness and a center-selected branch can disappear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Center stability holds for \(\varepsilon>0\), but uniqueness can fail at \(\varepsilon=0\).

notation.meaning: regularized solution with parameter epsilon and center z

children.title: Structured Primal–Dual Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step PDHG for a convex composite problem on real Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex functions, and let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded and linear. Consider \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)+g(Kx)\). Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\), initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k\geq0\), iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.\] Stop at a prescribed primal-dual residual tolerance or iteration limit and output the final pair \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PDHG alternates a dual proximal step, a primal proximal step, and primal extrapolation under a coupled step-size condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm generates primal-dual iterates \((x^k,y^k)\in X\times Y\).

children.title: Preconditioned Primal–Dual Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG with strongly positive primal and dual metric operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex functions, and let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded and linear. Consider \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)+g(Kx)\). Let \(T:X\to X\) and \(S:Y\to Y\) be bounded, self-adjoint, strongly positive operators satisfying \(\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\). Initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k\geq0\), iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{S^{-1}}_{g^*}(y^k+SK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_f(x^k-TK^*y^{k+1}),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.\] Here, for a strongly positive operator \(M\), \[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_h(v)=\arg\min_u\left\{h(u)+\tfrac12\langle M(u-v),u-v\rangle\right\}.\] Stop at a prescribed metric primal-dual residual tolerance or iteration limit and output the final pair \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned PDHG replaces scalar step sizes by compatible strongly positive primal and dual metrics while retaining proximal primal-dual updates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
\(T\) and \(S\) are bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric proximal updates are uniquely defined and generate iterates \((x^k,y^k)\in X\times Y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity-accelerated PDHG with coupled variable step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the PDHG model and that \(f\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex with \(\gamma>0\). Choose \(\tau_0,\sigma_0>0\) satisfying \(\tau_0\sigma_0\|K\|^2<1\), initialize \(x^0,y^0\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_k g^*}(y^k+\sigma_kK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau_k f}(x^k-\tau_kK^*y^{k+1}),\] then set \(\theta_k=(1+2\gamma\tau_k)^{-1/2}\), \(\tau_{k+1}=\theta_k\tau_k\), \(\sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k/\theta_k\), and \(\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta_k(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Return the final primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity permits coupled shrinking primal steps, expanding dual steps, and extrapolation in an accelerated PDHG schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update preserves \(\tau_k\sigma_k=\tau_0\sigma_0\) while applying accelerated extrapolation.

notation.meaning: variable primal and dual step sizes

children.title: Accelerated Preconditioning Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Preconditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric compatibility condition for accelerated primal–dual rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_k\succ0\) and \(S_k\succ0\) be primal and dual metrics for a bounded linear coupling \(K\). An accelerated reciprocal-rescaling regime is admissible when there exist \(\delta>0\) and factors \(\theta_k\in(0,1]\) such that \[T_{k+1}=\theta_kT_k,\qquad S_{k+1}=\theta_k^{-1}S_k,\qquad \|S_k^{1/2}KT_k^{1/2}\|\leq1-\delta\quad\forall k.\] The reciprocal scaling preserves the scalar product \(\tau_k\sigma_k\) in the scalar-metric case and keeps the primal-dual coupling uniformly inside the stability boundary; the choice of \(\theta_k\) must additionally match the strong-convexity modulus used by the accelerated update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration-compatible metrics are reciprocally rescaled while their preconditioned coupling norm remains uniformly below one.
assumptions_latex: \(T_k\) and \(S_k\) are bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.

children.title: Randomized Primal–Dual Methods
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual methods using randomized coordinate, component, or operator access.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized coordinate activation of an averaged primal-dual fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(Z=Z_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Z_m\), and let \(P_i:Z\to Z\) be the orthogonal projection onto block \(i\). Let \(R:Z\to Z\) be an \(\alpha\)-averaged map, with \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), whose fixed points encode the target KKT system. Choose probabilities \(p_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\), initialize \(z^0\in Z\), and at iteration \(k\) sample \(i_k\) independently of the past with \(\mathbb{P}(i_k=i)=p_i\). Given \(\lambda_k>0\), update \[z^{k+1}=z^k+\frac{\lambda_k}{p_{i_k}}P_{i_k}\bigl(Rz^k-z^k\bigr).\] Then \[\mathbb{E}[z^{k+1}-z^k\mid z^k]=\lambda_k(Rz^k-z^k).\] Stop when a prescribed sampled or expected fixed-point residual meets tolerance, or at an iteration limit, and output the final \(z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized primal-dual iteration activates one block of an averaged KKT fixed-point map; inverse-probability scaling makes the update direction conditionally unbiased.
assumptions_latex: The samples \(i_k\) are independent of the past.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[z^{k+1}-z^k\mid z^k]=\lambda_k(Rz^k-z^k)\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projection onto product-space block i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Randomized block-update distance identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-distance identities relating one randomized block update to the corresponding full proximal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \widehat{\mathbf x}^{0}=\mathbf x^{0} and, for t=1,\ldots,s, define \widehat{\mathbf x}^{t}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in X}\left\{\psi(\mathbf x)+\langle \mathbf A^{\top}y^{t},\mathbf x\rangle+\frac{\eta_t}{2}\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^{t-1}\|^{2}\right\}, where \mathbf x^{t} and y^{t} are obtained from (6.6.53)–(6.6.54). Then, for \mathbf x\in X, \mathbb E_{i_t}\!\left[\|\mathbf x-\widehat{\mathbf x}^{t}\|^{2}\right]=\mathbb E_{i_t}\!\left[(m-1)\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^{t}\|^{2}-(m-2)\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^{t-1}\|^{2}\right] and \mathbb E_{i_t}\!\left[\|\widehat{\mathbf x}^{t}-\mathbf x^{t-1}\|^{2}\right]=\mathbb E_{i_t}\!\left[(m-1)\|x_{i_t}^{t}-x_{i_t}^{t-1}\|^{2}\right].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each randomized block iteration, the expected squared distance to the full proximal minimizer equals a weighted difference of the current and preceding iterate distances. The expected full proximal-step length squared equals m−1 times the selected block-step length squared.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate PDHG for separable dual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(K_ix)\), with proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(f,g_i\). Choose primal step \(\tau>0\), dual steps \(\sigma_i>0\), initialize \(x^0,y_i^0\), and choose nonempty active sets \(I_k\). For \(i\in I_k\), set \(y_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_i g_i^*}(y_i^k+\sigma_iK_i\bar x^k)\); for \(i\notin I_k\), set \(y_i^{k+1}=y_i^k\). Then compute \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\left(x^k-\tau\sum_{i=1}^mK_i^*y_i^{k+1}\right),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.\] Stop by a blockwise KKT residual and return \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block PDHG updates selected dual blocks, retains inactive blocks, and then performs one primal proximal step using all current dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
The active-set schedule visits every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration updates \(y_i\) only for \(i\in I_k\) and updates the shared primal variable once.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Block Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased and exhaustive sampling condition for block primal–dual updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{F}_k\) be the history before iteration \(k\), and let \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the sampled active set. Define conditional inclusion probabilities \(p_{i,k}=\mathbb{P}(i\in I_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k)\). A randomized block rule is admissible when \[p_{i,k}\geq p_{\min}>0\qquad\text{almost surely for every }i,k.\] For block vectors \(d=(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\), the probability-corrected estimator \(\widehat d_k\), defined by \((\widehat d_k)_i=\mathbf{1}_{\{i\in I_k\}}d_i/p_{i,k}\), then satisfies \[\mathbb{E}[\widehat d_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=d.\] Positive lower-bounded inclusion probabilities also prevent any block from being permanently excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every block must have uniformly positive conditional selection probability; inverse-probability scaling then makes the sampled block direction unbiased.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat d_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=d\).

notation.meaning: conditional inclusion probability of block i

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-type projection for a constrained variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C	o X^*\), and let \(h:C	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strongly convex. Define \(D_h(x,z)=h(x)-h(z)-\langle
abla h(z),x-zangle\). Given \(x^0\in C\) and step sizes \(\gamma_k>0\), compute \[x^{k+1}=\arg\min_{x\in C}\left\{\gamma_k\langle F(x^k),xangle+D_h(x,x^k)ight\}.\] Equivalently, \(x^{k+1}\) satisfies \(\langle\gamma_kF(x^k)+
abla h(x^{k+1})-
abla h(x^k),x-x^{k+1}angle\geq0\) for all \(x\in C\). Stop by a Bregman-gradient residual or iteration limit and return the last iterate or a prescribed weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman projection step minimizes a linearized VI field plus Bregman distance, replacing Euclidean projection by geometry generated by a strongly convex function.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on C.

children.title: Bregman Prox Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal VI methods using Bregman distance generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Prox Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite Bregman proximal step for a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let \(C\subset X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(r:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. Let \(h:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex on an open set \(U\supset C\), and define \(D_h(u,v)=h(u)-h(v)-\langle\nabla h(v),u-v\rangle\) for \(u,v\in C\). Given \(x_0\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}r\), stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), and values \(g_k\in X^*\), assume that each displayed subproblem has a unique minimizer and compute
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\eta_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+\eta_k r(x)+D_h(x,x_k)\right\},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.
\]
Stop when a prescribed residual or iteration budget is reached, and output the last iterate or a specified weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize a linear term generated by a dual-space value, the convex nonsmooth term, and the Bregman distance from the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real normed space and \(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Each displayed subproblem has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is the Bregman proximal update generated by \(g_k\) with stepsize \(\eta_k\).

notation.meaning: dual-space operator evaluation or subgradient used at iteration k

children.title: Bregman Geometry Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of distance generators, constraint geometry, and proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Geometry Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions ensuring well-defined Bregman proximal VI steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let \(C\subset X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(r:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. A function \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is compatible with \(C\) and \(r\) for these Bregman proximal steps when \(C\subset\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), \(h\) is continuously differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(C\) for some \(\mu>0\), and, with
\[
D_h(x,z)=h(x)-h(z)-\langle\nabla h(z),x-z\rangle,
\]
the problem
\[
\min_{x\in C}\left\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+\eta r(x)+D_h(x,z)\right\}
\]
attains its minimum for every \(z\in C\), \(g\in X^*\), and \(\eta>0\). Strong convexity makes the minimizer unique and gives \(D_h(x,z)\geq \frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x-z\rVert^2\) for all \(x,z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility requires a differentiable strongly convex generator whose Bregman proximal subproblems over the feasible set attain unique solutions and whose divergence controls squared norm distance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real normed space and \(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Bregman proximal mapping is single-valued on its stated domain and \(D_h\) controls squared norm distance.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of h on C

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained VI Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional multiplier reduction of a linearly constrained variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(C\subset X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(F:C\to X^*\). Assume \(\operatorname{ri}C\cap\{x\in X:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\). For any \(x^\star\in C\) satisfying \(Ax^\star=b\), the variational inequality
\[
\langle F(x^\star),z-x^\star\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }z\in C\text{ satisfying }Az=b
\]
holds if and only if there exists \(y^\star\in Y^*\) such that
\[
0\in F(x^\star)+A^*y^\star+N_C(x^\star),\qquad Ax^\star=b.
\]
Thus the constrained variational inequality is represented by a primal-dual inclusion on \(X\times Y^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior constraint qualification, a linearly constrained variational inequality is equivalent to a primal-dual normal-cone inclusion with an equality multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(b\in Y\), and \(\operatorname{ri}C\cap\{x\in X:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible variational inequality and the displayed primal-dual inclusion have the same primal solutions.

children.title: Stochastic Extragradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Variants distinguished by sample reuse, independence, and batching.

children.title: Same-Sample Extragradient
children.top_down_role: Stochastic extragradient using coupled samples across prediction and correction evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Same-Sample Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic extragradient reusing one sample in both oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(G(z;\xi)\) be a stochastic oracle for \(F(z)\). Given \(z_0\in C\) and stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), draw one sample \(\xi_k\) at iteration \(k\) and compute
\[
y_k=P_C\bigl(z_k-\eta_kG(z_k;\xi_k)\bigr),\qquad
z_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(z_k-\eta_kG(y_k;\xi_k)\bigr).
\]
The identical realization \(\xi_k\) is used in the prediction and correction calls. Stop according to a prescribed residual or budget and output the last iterate or a stated average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each extragradient iteration draws one sample and reuses it for both the prediction and correction oracle evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(G(\cdot;\xi)\) is defined at both queried points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updates define the same-sample projected stochastic extragradient iteration.

notation.meaning: sample reused by both oracle calls at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed two-call sample reuse is the defining same-sample coupling regime
