intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed recursion correctly represents the same-sample coupling regime and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Independent-Sample Extragradient
children.top_down_role: Stochastic extragradient using separate samples across prediction and correction evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Sample Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic extragradient with independent prediction and correction samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(G(z;\xi)\) be a stochastic oracle for \(F(z)\). Given \(z_0\in C\) and \(\eta_k>0\), draw conditionally independent samples \(\xi_k\) and \(\xi'_k\), independently of the past, and compute
\[
y_k=P_C\bigl(z_k-\eta_kG(z_k;\xi_k)\bigr),\qquad
z_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(z_k-\eta_kG(y_k;\xi'_k)\bigr).
\]
Stop according to a prescribed residual or budget and output the last iterate or a specified average. Independence separates the correction noise from the random prediction point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prediction and correction use separate conditionally independent samples, making the correction oracle unbiased conditional on the prediction point.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi'_k\) is conditionally independent of \(y_k\) given the past.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[G(y_k;\xi'_k)\mid y_k]=F(y_k)\), and the displayed updates define independent-sample extragradient.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional independence directly yields the displayed conditional expectation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The independent-sample recursion and conditional-unbiasedness statement are coherent, but the record has no citation supporting this stochastic VI formulation.

children.title: Sample-Coupling Effects
children.top_down_role: Bias, variance, and dependence consequences of coupling the two oracle evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Coupling Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-bias distinction between same-sample and independent-sample correction calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\mathbb{E}[G(z;\xi)]=F(z)\) for every deterministic \(z\). If \(y=P_C(z-\eta G(z;\xi))\), then \(y\) depends on \(\xi\), so marginal unbiasedness does not generally imply
\[
\mathbb{E}[G(y;\xi)\mid y]=F(y).
\]
If a fresh sample \(\xi'\) is independent of \((y,\xi)\), then
\[
\mathbb{E}[G(y;\xi')\mid y]=F(y).
\]
Consequently, reusing the prediction sample can create conditional correction bias and correlated errors, whereas independent sampling removes that particular bias, though it requires an additional independent draw.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing a sample can bias the correction conditional on the prediction point; a fresh independent sample restores conditional unbiasedness.
assumptions_latex: \(G(z;\xi)\) is integrable and marginally unbiased for each deterministic \(z\).
\(y\) is measurable with respect to the prediction sample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent correction sampling guarantees conditional unbiasedness; same-sample correction need not satisfy it.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is a direct conditional-expectation distinction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-bias distinction is mathematically plausible and the property kind fits the leaf, but the claimed same-sample effect requires an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Mini-Batch Extragradient
children.top_down_role: Extragradient methods using multiple samples per operator estimate.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected extragradient using fixed-size averaged stochastic oracle batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Fix batch sizes \(b_1,b_2\geq1\). At iteration \(k\), draw independent samples \(\{\xi_{k,j}\}_{j=1}^{b_1}\) and \(\{\zeta_{k,j}\}_{j=1}^{b_2}\), define
\[
\widehat F_k(z_k)=\frac1{b_1}\sum_{j=1}^{b_1}G(z_k;\xi_{k,j}),\qquad y_k=P_C(z_k-\eta_k\widehat F_k(z_k)),
\]
and then set
\[
\widehat F'_k(y_k)=\frac1{b_2}\sum_{j=1}^{b_2}G(y_k;\zeta_{k,j}),\qquad z_{k+1}=P_C(z_k-\eta_k\widehat F'_k(y_k)).
\]
Stop at the prescribed budget and output the designated iterate or average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both extragradient oracle calls are replaced by averages over fixed-size independent mini-batches.
assumptions_latex: Samples within and between the two batches are independent conditional on the past.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed updates define fixed-mini-batch projected stochastic extragradient.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mini-batching is defined by averaging independent oracle samples in each call
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-mini-batch extragradient algorithm is internally consistent, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Increasing-Batch Extragradient
children.top_down_role: Extragradient methods whose sample counts grow across iterations or stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Increasing-Batch Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected extragradient with iteration-dependent batch sizes tending upward.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Choose positive stepsizes \(\eta_k\) and batch sizes \(b_k,c_k\) with \(b_k\to\infty\) and \(c_k\to\infty\). At iteration \(k\), form independent averages
\[
\widehat F_k(z_k)=\frac1{b_k}\sum_{j=1}^{b_k}G(z_k;\xi_{k,j}),\qquad y_k=P_C(z_k-\eta_k\widehat F_k(z_k)),
\]
\[
\widehat F'_k(y_k)=\frac1{c_k}\sum_{j=1}^{c_k}G(y_k;\zeta_{k,j}),\qquad z_{k+1}=P_C(z_k-\eta_k\widehat F'_k(y_k)).
\]
Stop at the prescribed total oracle budget and output the designated iterate or average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient batch sizes increase with the iteration, progressively reducing stochastic error while raising per-iteration oracle cost.
assumptions_latex: \(G(z;\xi)\) is unbiased with finite second moment.
All batch samples are conditionally independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion is increasing-batch stochastic extragradient, with estimator variances decreasing as batch sizes grow.

notation.meaning: iteration-dependent prediction and correction batch sizes

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: increasing-batch extragradient is specified by divergent batch schedules in both calls
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The increasing-batch recursion fits the leaf, but the assertion that estimator variances decrease across iterations needs a uniform conditional variance bound or a more qualified formulation, as well as an authoritative source.

children.title: Batch-Growth Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Oracle-cost and variance tradeoffs induced by changing batch sizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Growth Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance and oracle-cost accounting for batched extragradient calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume independent unbiased oracle samples satisfy \(\mathbb{E}\lVert G(z;\xi)-F(z)\rVert^2\leq\sigma^2\). For the average \(\widehat F_b(z)=b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^bG(z;\xi_j)\),
\[
\mathbb{E}\lVert\widehat F_b(z)-F(z)\rVert^2\leq\frac{\sigma^2}{b}.
\]
An extragradient iteration using batch sizes \(b_k\) and \(c_k\) consumes \(b_k+c_k\) stochastic oracle calls and has prediction and correction mean-square errors bounded by \(\sigma^2/b_k\) and \(\sigma^2/c_k\), respectively. Thus larger batches reduce sampling error inversely with batch size but increase total oracle work linearly; parallel hardware may reduce wall-clock time without reducing oracle count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch of size b divides mean-square oracle noise by b but multiplies sample-oracle work by b.
assumptions_latex: Oracle errors are independent within each batch.
The oracle error has uniformly bounded second moment \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Variance scales as \(O(1/b)\), while stochastic oracle count scales as \(O(b)\) per batched call.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variance-of-an-independent-average and exact oracle counting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Independent averaging gives the stated inverse-batch variance accounting in a Hilbert or Euclidean setting, but the ambient space and norm are not introduced and no cited source supports the complexity statement.

children.title: Variance-Reduced VI Methods
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum and recursive-estimator corrections for stochastic operator problems.

children.title: Snapshot-Based VI Methods
children.top_down_role: Variance-reduced VI methods using periodically refreshed reference snapshots.

knowledge_statements.title: Snapshot-Based VI Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum VI estimator using periodically refreshed full-operator snapshots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(z)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF_i(z)\). At a refresh time choose a snapshot \(\widetilde z\) and compute \(F(\widetilde z)\) using all \(n\) components. For an inner oracle call at \(z\), sample \(i\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and use
\[
v(z;i)=F_i(z)-F_i(\widetilde z)+F(\widetilde z).
\]
Insert \(v(z;i)\) into the chosen projected, proximal, or extragradient VI update. After a fixed inner-loop length or a stated random refresh event, replace \(\widetilde z\) and recompute its full operator. Output the iterate or average prescribed by the underlying VI method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A periodically refreshed full-operator snapshot anchors a component-difference estimator that is unbiased for the current finite-sum operator.
assumptions_latex: The component index is sampled uniformly.
The full snapshot value is computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}_i[v(z;i)]=F(z)\), so the snapshot estimator is unbiased.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the estimator identity follows exactly from uniform finite-sum sampling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The snapshot estimator is unbiased under uniform finite-sum sampling and algorithm is the correct role, but no authoritative variance-reduced VI source is cited.

children.title: Table-Based VI Methods
children.top_down_role: Variance-reduced VI methods maintaining component-wise stored information.

knowledge_statements.title: Table-Based VI Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum VI estimator maintaining and incrementally refreshing component memories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(z)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF_i(z)\). Maintain stored vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\) and their average \(\bar a=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^na_j\). At an oracle call at \(z\), sample \(i\) uniformly and form
\[
v(z;i)=F_i(z)-a_i+\bar a.
\]
Use \(v(z;i)\) in the selected VI update, then refresh the sampled entry by setting \(a_i^+=F_i(z)\), leave \(a_j^+=a_j\) for \(j\neq i\), and update
\[
\bar a^+=\bar a+\frac1n(a_i^+-a_i).
\]
Stop under the underlying method's criterion and output its designated iterate or average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A table stores component operator values; one sampled entry is corrected and refreshed per oracle call while the running average is updated.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index is uniform conditional on the current table.
The table is initialized with defined component values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditionally on \(z\) and the table, \(\mathbb{E}_i[v(z;i)]=F(z)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the table estimator and its conditional unbiasedness follow by finite-sum averaging
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The table estimator, incremental average update, and conditional-unbiasedness identity are coherent, but the record lacks an inspectable source specific to table-based VI methods.

children.title: Memory–Refresh Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Storage, refresh frequency, and estimator-quality distinctions between the two families.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory–Refresh Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and refresh costs of snapshot-based versus table-based finite-sum estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF_i\) with vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), a snapshot estimator stores \(\widetilde z\) and \(F(\widetilde z)\), requiring \(O(d)\) vector memory, but each exact refresh evaluates all \(n\) components. Between refreshes, each estimator call evaluates the sampled component at the current and snapshot points unless snapshot component values are additionally stored. A table estimator stores \(n\) component vectors, requiring \(O(nd)\) memory, and refreshes one entry per sampled call in \(O(d)\) table-update work. Hence snapshot schemes trade periodic \(O(n)\) refresh cost for low memory, while table schemes trade \(O(nd)\) memory for incremental refresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Snapshot methods use little memory but periodically compute all components; table methods store all component values and refresh them incrementally.
assumptions_latex: Each component operator value is a vector in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
Complexity counts stored scalars and component-operator evaluations.
No additional component cache is charged to the basic snapshot scheme.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Basic snapshot storage is \(O(d)\) with \(n\)-evaluation full refreshes, whereas table storage is \(O(nd)\) with one-entry incremental refreshes.

notation.meaning: dimension of each stored operator vector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounds follow from explicit storage and component-evaluation accounting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated storage and refresh accounting is valid for the explicitly described basic implementations, and complexity_bound fits the tradeoff leaf, but the claims are implementation-dependent and have no authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive-Estimator VI Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum projected extragradient with periodic full-operator refreshes and recursive component-difference estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F(z)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n F_i(z)\). Given \(z_0\in C\), stepsize \(\gamma>0\), and refresh period \(q\ge 1\), set \(v_0=F(z_0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \(y_k=P_C(z_k-\gamma v_k)\), sample \(i_k\) uniformly, set \(w_k=v_k+F_{i_k}(y_k)-F_{i_k}(z_k)\), and compute \(z_{k+1}=P_C(z_k-\gamma w_k)\). If \(k+1\) is a multiple of \(q\), set \(v_{k+1}=F(z_{k+1})\); otherwise sample \(j_k\) uniformly and set \(v_{k+1}=w_k+F_{j_k}(z_{k+1})-F_{j_k}(y_k)\). Stop by a prescribed budget or residual test and return an ergodic average of \(y_k\) or the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected extragradient uses recursively updated component-difference estimates between periodic exact finite-sum refreshes, returning an ergodic average or final iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n F_i\), and queried component indices are sampled uniformly.
All displayed component values and Euclidean projections are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k,y_k\in C\) for every generated iteration, while full evaluations of \(F\) occur only at refresh iterations.

notation.meaning: recursive operator estimates at the base and extrapolated points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and leaf placement are appropriate, but the particular two-stage recursive estimator, refresh schedule, output convention, and index-sampling dependencies have no cited source. Algorithm-specific evidence is required before the mathematical variant can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Controlled-Error Oracle Methods
children.top_down_role: Method families and analyses organized around controlled evaluation error and oracle bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic-Error Extragradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean extragradient driven by deterministically bounded additive operator errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Suppose an inexact oracle returns \(\widetilde F_k(x)=F(x)+e_k(x)\) with \(\|e_k(x)\|\le\delta_k\) at every queried \(x\in C\). Given \(z_0\in C\) and stepsizes \(\gamma_k>0\), perform
\[y_k=P_C\!\left(z_k-\gamma_k\widetilde F_k(z_k)\right),\qquad z_{k+1}=P_C\!\left(z_k-\gamma_k\widetilde F_k(y_k)\right).\]
The two calls may have distinct errors provided each obeys the stated bound. Stop after \(K\) iterations or when a prescribed residual tolerance holds, and return \(\bar y_K=(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k y_k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k)\), or the last iterate when a last-iterate guarantee is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient replaces both exact operator calls by approximations whose additive errors obey deterministic iterationwise bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle error satisfies \(\|e_k(x)\|\le\delta_k\) at queried points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k,z_{k+1}\in C\), and \(\bar y_K\in C\) whenever \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record is a correctly scoped algorithm description and makes no unsupported convergence-rate claim, but no source supports this deterministic additive-error formulation, its two-call convention, or its output rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Biased-Oracle Mirror-Prox
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-Prox updates with conditionally biased stochastic operator observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space and let \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strongly convex. Define \(P_x(g)=\arg\min_{u\in C}\{\langle g,u\rangle+D_h(u,x)\}\). Given \(z_0\in C\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), query \(G_k(z_k)\), set \(y_k=P_{z_k}(\gamma_kG_k(z_k))\), query \(G'_k(y_k)\), and set \(z_{k+1}=P_{z_k}(\gamma_kG'_k(y_k))\). The oracle may be biased: conditionally on the past, \(\mathbb E[G_k(x)]=F(x)+b_k(x)\) and \(\|b_k(x)\|_*\le\beta_k\), with the analogous condition for \(G'_k\). After \(K\) steps return \(\bar y_K=(\sum_{k<K}\gamma_k y_k)/(\sum_{k<K}\gamma_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-Prox permits conditional oracle bias bounded in dual norm and returns a stepsize-weighted average of extrapolation points.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex, and \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(C\).
The conditional bias at each queried point is bounded by \(\beta_k\) in the dual norm.
Each prox subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k,z_{k+1}\in C\), and the oracle discrepancy decomposes into bounded conditional bias plus a conditionally mean-zero component.

notation.meaning: Bregman proximal mapping based at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic match, but a source is needed to validate the precise conditional-bias model, filtration-dependent oracle calls, and Mirror-Prox update convention. The Bregman divergence should also be explicitly defined once a sourced formulation is selected.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Oracle Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic ergodic VI bound obtained by telescoping per-iteration inexact prox inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be convex, \(F:C\to E^*\), and suppose points \(y_k\in C\), weights \(\gamma_k>0\), potentials \(V_k(u)\ge0\), and errors \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) satisfy, for every \(u\in C\),
\[\gamma_k\langle F(y_k),y_k-u\rangle\le V_k(u)-V_{k+1}(u)+\gamma_k\varepsilon_k.\]
Writing \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k\) and \(\bar y_K=S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k y_k\), summation yields
\[\sup_{u\in C}\frac{1}{S_K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k\langle F(y_k),y_k-u\rangle\le\frac{\sup_{u\in C}V_0(u)}{S_K}+\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma_k\varepsilon_k}{S_K},\]
provided \(\sup_{u\in C}V_0(u)<\infty\). Thus inexactness accumulates as a stepsize-weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A telescoping exact-method term decays with total stepsize, while inexact oracle losses accumulate as their stepsize-weighted average.
assumptions_latex: The displayed one-step inequality holds for every \(u\in C\) and \(k<K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_{u\in C}S_K^{-1}\sum_{k<K}\gamma_k\langle F(y_k),y_k-u\rangle\le S_K^{-1}\sup_{u\in C}V_0(u)+S_K^{-1}\sum_{k<K}\gamma_k\varepsilon_k.\)

notation.meaning: nonnegative analysis potential relative to test point u
additive inexactness loss at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping inequality and weighted-error accumulation are mathematically coherent and the complexity-bound role fits the leaf, but the nontrivial bound has no cited evidence.

children.title: Robust Stochastic Operator Methods
children.top_down_role: Saddle-specific robustification interfaces; generic clipped, normalized, and adaptive stochastic-gradient theories remain external.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Mean-Operator Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise geometric median-of-means estimation for a stochastic VI operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a query point \(z\), suppose \(G(z,\xi_1),\ldots,G(z,\xi_N)\) are independent observations in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with mean \(F(z)\). Partition the indices into \(B\ge3\) nonempty blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_B\), form block means \(m_b(z)=|I_b|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_b}G(z,\xi_i)\), and return
\[\widehat F_{\mathrm{rob}}(z)\in\arg\min_{v}\sum_{b=1}^B\|v-m_b(z)\|.\]
This estimator replaces a raw sample mean at each operator interface. Its stopping rule is the termination criterion of the outer VI method; numerical computation of the geometric median must meet a prescribed inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition independent operator samples into blocks, average within blocks, and return a geometric median of the block means.
assumptions_latex: The operator samples at the queried point are independent and have common mean \(F(z)\).
The ambient space is finite-dimensional and Hilbertian.
The sample blocks are nonempty and disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F_{\mathrm{rob}}(z)\) is a geometric median of the blockwise operator means.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric median-of-means construction is appropriately classified as an algorithm, but no source supports this pointwise operator-estimation interface, the block convention, or the stated integration with an outer VI method.

children.title: Clipped Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Operator interfaces that truncate extreme evaluations for robust stochastic processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Clipped Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial clipping of an operator observation at a prescribed norm threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((E,\|\cdot\|)\) be a normed space and let \(\tau>0\). The clipped interface \(T_\tau:E\to E\) is
\[T_\tau(v)=v\min\left\{1,\frac{\tau}{\|v\|}\right\}\quad\text{for }v\ne0,\qquad T_\tau(0)=0.\]
For an operator observation \(G(z,\xi)\in E\), the interface supplies \(\widetilde G_\tau(z,\xi)=T_\tau(G(z,\xi))\) to the VI update. It leaves observations with norm at most \(\tau\) unchanged and radially rescales larger observations to norm \(\tau\). Consequently \(\|\widetilde G_\tau(z,\xi)\|\le\tau\) for every input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radial clipping preserves observations below a threshold and rescales larger ones to have exactly the threshold norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|T_\tau(v)\|=\min\{\|v\|,\tau\}\) for every \(v\in E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The radial clipping definition is precise, internally consistent, and correctly placed, but the record contains a nontrivial transformation claim without any cited source.

children.title: Normalized Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Operator interfaces that rescale evaluations by magnitude or adaptive scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft radial normalization producing uniformly bounded operator observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((E,\|\cdot\|)\) be a normed space and fix \(\tau>0\). Define the soft-normalized interface \(N_\tau:E\to E\) by
\[N_\tau(v)=\frac{v}{1+\|v\|/\tau}.\]
For a stochastic operator observation \(G(z,\xi)\), the transformed observation is \(\widetilde G_\tau(z,\xi)=N_\tau(G(z,\xi))\). The transformation preserves direction, continuously shrinks every nonzero input, and satisfies
\[\|N_\tau(v)\|=\frac{\tau\|v\|}{\tau+\|v\|}<\tau\quad\text{for }v\ne0.\]
Thus the outer VI method receives a bounded observation without a discontinuity in the radial scaling factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft normalization preserves direction while smoothly shrinking every operator observation to norm strictly below a chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|N_\tau(v)\|=\tau\|v\|/(\tau+\|v\|)\le\tau\) for every \(v\in E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and norm identity are correct for the stated soft-normalization convention, but multiple normalization conventions exist and no source identifies this one as the intended interface.

children.title: Robustness–Distortion Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Bias, scale sensitivity, and information-loss boundaries introduced by robust transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness–Distortion Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias and boundedness induced by radial clipping of a random operator observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be an integrable random vector in a normed space, let \(F=\mathbb E[G]\), and let \(T_\tau\) be radial clipping at \(\tau>0\). Then
\[\|T_\tau(G)\|\le\tau,\qquad \|\mathbb E[T_\tau(G)]-F\|\le\mathbb E\big[(\|G\|-\tau)_+\big].\]
Hence clipping gives a deterministic bound on every transformed observation but generally changes its mean. Increasing \(\tau\) decreases the displayed distortion upper bound while weakening the uniform magnitude control. If \(\mathbb E\|G\|^p<\infty\) for some \(p>1\), then
\[\mathbb E[(\|G\|-\tau)_+]\le\frac{\mathbb E\|G\|^p}{\tau^{p-1}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping bounds every observation by the threshold, while its induced mean bias is controlled by the discarded norm tail.
assumptions_latex: For the moment bound, \(\mathbb E\|G\|^p<\infty\) for some \(p>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\mathbb E[T_\tau(G)]-\mathbb E[G]\|\le\mathbb E[(\|G\|-\tau)_+]\le\tau^{1-p}\mathbb E\|G\|^p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundedness, clipping-bias estimate, and moment-tail bound are mathematically consistent and the property role fits the tradeoff leaf, but these nontrivial claims have no cited evidence.

children.title: Saddle-Point Gap Functions
children.top_down_role: Gap certificates expressed directly through opposing saddle objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global saddle residual for a convex–concave function on a product domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty convex sets and let \(L:X\times Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). At \((x,y)\in X\times Y\), define the saddle-point gap
\[\mathcal G_L(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y).\]
Whenever both terms are finite, \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)\ge0\). Moreover, \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)=0\) if and only if
\[L(x,v)\le L(x,y)\le L(u,y)\qquad\text{for all }u\in X,\ v\in Y,\]
so a finite zero gap certifies that \((x,y)\) is a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The saddle gap compares the worst opposing value at each coordinate; a finite zero gap exactly certifies a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is convex in its first argument and concave in its second.
The defining supremum and infimum are finite at the evaluated pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)\ge0\), with \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)=0\) exactly when \((x,y)\) satisfies the global saddle inequalities.

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Functions
children.top_down_role: Gap certificates expressed through primal and dual objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality residual for a convex primal problem and its Fenchel dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(g:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, closed, convex functions between finite-dimensional spaces, and let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear. Define
\[P(x)=f(x)+g(Kx),\qquad D(y)=-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(y).\]
For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}P\) and \(y\in\operatorname{dom}(-D)\), the primal–dual gap is
\[\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=f(x)+g(Kx)+f^*(-K^*y)+g^*(y).\]
Weak duality gives \(\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y)\ge0\). A zero gap certifies simultaneous primal and dual optimality whenever the primal and dual optimal values coincide and are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal–dual gap is the feasible primal value minus the feasible dual value; under attained strong duality, zero certifies optimality of both.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex on finite-dimensional spaces.
\(K\) is linear, and the displayed primal and dual values are finite.
For the zero-gap certificate, strong duality holds and both optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y)\ge0\); under attained strong duality, \(\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y)=0\) implies that \(x\) and \(y\) are primal and dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Error Bound from an Excessive-Gap Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An excessive-gap inequality for bounded smoothing approximations yields simultaneous primal, dual, and primal–dual objective-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume f^*=\min_{x\in Q_1}f(x)=\max_{u\in Q_2}\phi(u), D_1:=\max_{x\in Q_1}d_1(x)<\infty, and D_2:=\max_{u\in Q_2}d_2(u)<\infty. Let \mu_1,\mu_2>0, and suppose f(x)-\mu_2D_2\le f_{\mu_2}(x)\le f(x) for every x\in Q_1 and \phi(u)\le\phi_{\mu_1}(u)\le\phi(u)+\mu_1D_1 for every u\in Q_2. If \bar{x}\in Q_1 and \bar{u}\in Q_2 satisfy f_{\mu_2}(\bar{x})\le\phi_{\mu_1}(\bar{u}), then 0\le\max\{f(\bar{x})-f^*,f^*-\phi(\bar{u})\}\le f(\bar{x})-\phi(\bar{u})\le\mu_1D_1+\mu_2D_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal and dual optimal values agree and both smoothing errors are bounded by finite prox diameters, an excessive-gap pair has primal and dual objective errors no larger than its actual primal–dual gap, which is at most the weighted sum of those diameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\max\{f(\bar{x})-f^*,\ f^*-\phi(\bar{u})\}\le f(\bar{x})-\phi(\bar{u})\le\mu_1D_1+\mu_2D_2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Excessive-Gap Primal-Dual Error Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the original primal-dual gap and both one-sided objective errors using the smoothing parameters and bounded prox-function values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume
\[
f^*=\min_{x\in Q_1}f(x)=\max_{u\in Q_2}\phi(u),
\]
and let
\[
D_1:=\max_{x\in Q_1}d_1(x)<\infty,\qquad D_2:=\max_{u\in Q_2}d_2(u)<\infty.
\]
For $\mu_1,\mu_2>0$, define
\[
f_{\mu_2}(x):=f(x)-\mu_2d_2(u_x),\qquad \phi_{\mu_1}(u):=\phi(u)+\mu_1d_1(x_u),
\]
with the quantities on the right chosen so that, for all $x\in Q_1$ and $u\in Q_2$,
\[
f(x)-\mu_2D_2\le f_{\mu_2}(x)\le f(x),\qquad \phi(u)\le\phi_{\mu_1}(u)\le\phi(u)+\mu_1D_1.
\]
If $f_{\mu_2}(\bar x)\le\phi_{\mu_1}(\bar u)$, then
\[
0\le\max\{f(\bar x)-f^*,\,f^*-\phi(\bar u)\}\le f(\bar x)-\phi(\bar u)\le\mu_1D_1+\mu_2D_2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal and dual optimal values agree, the prox-function values are bounded, and the stated smoothing-error bounds hold, an excessive-gap pair has original primal-dual gap at most the sum of the two smoothing errors. This gap also bounds both one-sided objective errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\max\{f(\bar x)-f^*,f^*-\phi(\bar u)\}\le f(\bar x)-\phi(\bar u)\le\mu_1D_1+\mu_2D_2

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-to-Primal–Dual Gap Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between Fenchel saddle gaps and primal–dual gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) and \(g\) be proper, closed, convex functions on finite-dimensional spaces, let \(K\) be linear, and define
\[L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y).\]
For every pair \((x,y)\) at which the quantities are finite,
\[\sup_v L(x,v)=f(x)+g(Kx)=P(x),\qquad \inf_u L(u,y)=-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(y)=D(y).\]
Consequently,
\[\mathcal G_L(x,y)=\sup_vL(x,v)-\inf_uL(u,y)=P(x)-D(y)=\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y).\]
Thus the global saddle-point and Fenchel primal–dual gaps give the same numerical certificate for this canonical saddle representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the canonical Fenchel saddle representation, maximizing and minimizing the saddle function recover the primal and dual objectives, so both gaps coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex on finite-dimensional spaces.
All displayed extrema and objective values are finite at \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)=\mathcal G_{PD}(x,y)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\), and let \(U\subseteq X\) and \(V\subseteq Y\) be nonempty test sets. For \((x,y)\in X\times Y\), define the restricted gap by
\[\mathcal G_{U,V}(x,y)=\sup_{v\in V}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in U}L(u,y),\]
whenever the displayed supremum and infimum are finite. If \(x\in U\) and \(y\in V\), then \(\mathcal G_{U,V}(x,y)\ge 0\). If \(U_1\subseteq U_2\) and \(V_1\subseteq V_2\), and all four gaps are finite, then
\[\mathcal G_{U_1,V_1}(x,y)\le \mathcal G_{U_2,V_2}(x,y).\]
Taking \(U=X\) and \(V=Y\) recovers the global saddle-point gap whenever it is finite; smaller test sets yield weaker certificates that may remain finite when the global gap is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted gap tests saddle inequalities only against chosen primal and dual subsets. At points belonging to both test sets it is nonnegative, and enlarging either test set can only increase any finite gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean convex–concave saddle gap localized by a comparator ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty closed convex sets, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second. For \(z=(x,y)\in X\times Y\) and \(r>0\), the radius-\(r\) localized saddle gap is
\[
G_r(z):=\sup_{(u,v)\in (X\times Y)\cap B(z,r)}\bigl(L(x,v)-L(u,y)\bigr).
\]
Because \((x,y)\) is an admissible comparator, \(G_r(z)\geq 0\). It measures the largest saddle inequality violation detectable by comparators within distance \(r\) of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The localized gap is the worst saddle inequality violation found by comparing the candidate only with feasible points lying in a prescribed neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(L\) is real-valued, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_r(z)=\sup_{(u,v)\in(X\times Y)\cap B(z,r)}[L(x,v)-L(u,y)]\geq 0\).

children.title: Restriction–Localization Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction–Localization Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and certificate strength under nested comparator restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\), and fix \((x,y)\in X\times Y\). For every nonempty comparator set \(S\subseteq X\times Y\), define
\[
G_S(x,y):=\sup_{(u,v)\in S}\bigl(L(x,v)-L(u,y)\bigr).
\]
If \(\varnothing\neq S_1\subseteq S_2\subseteq X\times Y\), then
\[
G_{S_1}(x,y)\leq G_{S_2}(x,y).
\]
Consequently, for \(S_r=(X\times Y)\cap B((x,y),r)\),
\[
0<r_1\leq r_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad G_{r_1}(x,y)\leq G_{r_2}(x,y).
\]
Thus restriction makes the gap no larger but tests fewer comparators. The restricted and unrestricted gaps are equal exactly when their suprema agree; if the unrestricted supremum is attained, inclusion of an unrestricted maximizer in the restricted set is sufficient for equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking the comparator set can only decrease the measured gap, producing an easier but weaker certificate unless the restricted set still captures the unrestricted supremum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{S_1}(x,y)\leq G_{S_2}(x,y)\); in particular, \(0<r_1\leq r_2\Rightarrow G_{r_1}(x,y)\leq G_{r_2}(x,y)\).

notation.meaning: Saddle gap restricted to comparator set S.
Feasible radius-r neighborhood of the evaluated point.

children.title: Primal VI Gaps
children.top_down_role: VI gap certificates organized around candidate-point operator evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal VI Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stampacchia, or regular, gap for a compact variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous. The primal variational-inequality gap is
\[
g_{\mathrm P}(x):=\max_{y\in C}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle ,\qquad x\in C.
\]
It is finite and nonnegative because \(y=x\) is feasible. Moreover, \(g_{\mathrm P}(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(x\) solves the Stampacchia variational inequality
\[
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq 0\qquad\text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal VI gap maximizes the current operator’s violation over feasible comparison points, and it vanishes exactly at Stampacchia VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm P}(x)\geq0\), and \(g_{\mathrm P}(x)=0\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for all \(y\in C\).

children.title: Dual VI Gaps
children.top_down_role: VI gap certificates organized around comparison-point operator evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual VI Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minty gap for a compact monotone variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous. The dual variational-inequality gap is
\[
g_{\mathrm D}(x):=\max_{y\in C}\langle F(y),x-y\rangle ,\qquad x\in C.
\]
It is finite and nonnegative. The identity \(g_{\mathrm D}(x)=0\) is equivalent to the Minty inequality \(\langle F(y),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in C\). If \(F\) is also monotone, continuity makes this condition equivalent to the Stampacchia variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual VI gap tests the candidate using operator values at comparison points; its zeros are Minty solutions and, under continuity and monotonicity, ordinary VI solutions.
assumptions_latex: For equivalence with Stampacchia solutions, \(F\) is monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm D}(x)=0\iff \langle F(y),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual gap for weak VI solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison-point-operator gap measuring violation of the weak variational-inequality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in X\), define \[g(\bar x):=\sup_{x\in X}\langle F(x),\bar x-x\rangle.\] Then \(g(\bar x)\ge0\). Furthermore, \[g(\bar x)=0\iff \langle F(x),x-\bar x\rangle\ge0\quad\forall x\in X,\] so a zero dual gap characterizes weak VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual VI gap is the worst comparison-point evaluation of the operator. It is nonnegative and equals zero exactly at weak VI solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)\) is defined for every \(x\in X\); the supremum is interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\bar x)\ge0\), and \(g(\bar x)=0\iff \langle F(x),x-\bar x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in X.\)

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Comparability
children.top_down_role: Regularity and domain regimes governing comparison of primal and dual VI gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise ordering and common zero set for monotone continuous VIs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous and monotone. For every \(x,y\in C\), monotonicity gives
\[
\langle F(y),x-y\rangle\leq\langle F(x),x-y\rangle.
\]
Taking maxima over \(y\) yields
\[
0\leq g_{\mathrm D}(x)\leq g_{\mathrm P}(x).
\]
Furthermore, continuity and monotonicity identify the Minty and Stampacchia solution sets, so \(g_{\mathrm D}(x)=0\) if and only if \(g_{\mathrm P}(x)=0\). This ordering alone supplies no uniform positive constant bounding \(g_{\mathrm P}\) by \(g_{\mathrm D}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous monotone VI, the dual gap never exceeds the primal gap, and both vanish at exactly the same feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq g_{\mathrm D}(x)\leq g_{\mathrm P}(x)\) and \(g_{\mathrm D}(x)=0\iff g_{\mathrm P}(x)=0\).

children.title: Regularized Gap Functions
children.top_down_role: Gap constructions modified by stabilizing or smoothing regularizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized primal gap for a Euclidean VI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(a>0\). The quadratically regularized gap is
\[
g_a(x):=\max_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{a}{2}\lVert x-y\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
The maximizer is unique and equals \(p_a(x)=P_C(x-a^{-1}F(x))\). Hence \(g_a(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(g_a(x)=0\) exactly when \(x=P_C(x-a^{-1}F(x))\), equivalently when \(x\) solves the variational inequality for \(F\) on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized VI gap subtracts a quadratic comparator penalty; its unique maximizing comparator is a projection, and the gap vanishes exactly at VI solutions.

notation.meaning: Gap with quadratic penalty parameter a.
Unique maximizing comparator for the regularized gap.

children.title: Linearized Gap Functions
children.top_down_role: Gap constructions based on local linearized comparison problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized gap induced by the affine VI model at a candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\neq\varnothing\) be a convex subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(x\in C\). The affine VI model against \(y\in C\) is
\[
\ell_x(y):=\langle F(x),y-x\rangle.
\]
Its linearized gap is the extended-real quantity
\[
g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x):=\sup_{y\in C}\bigl(-\ell_x(y)\bigr)=\sup_{y\in C}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle.
\]
It is nonnegative because \(y=x\) is feasible, although it may be infinite when \(C\) is unbounded. Moreover,
\[
g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq 0\quad\text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearized gap is the worst violation of the affine VI model at the candidate; it may be infinite on an unbounded feasible set and is zero exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x)=\sup_{y\in C}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle\geq0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).

notation.meaning: Affine VI model based at x.

children.title: Regularization–Linearization Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural connections and evaluation tradeoffs between the two transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization–Linearization Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic stabilization, projection representation, and residual lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the linearized gap \(g_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and its quadratic regularization \(g_a\), with \(a>0\), one has
\[
0\leq g_a(x)\leq g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x),
\]
where the upper bound is understood in the extended-real sense. If \(C\) is closed and convex and \(p_a(x)=P_C(x-a^{-1}F(x))\), then
\[
g_a(x)=\langle F(x),x-p_a(x)\rangle-\frac{a}{2}\lVert x-p_a(x)\rVert^2
\geq\frac{a}{2}\lVert x-p_a(x)\rVert^2.
\]
Thus quadratic regularization converts maximization of the affine model into a projection calculation while preserving the VI zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic regularization lowers the linearized gap, makes its maximizer a projection, and controls the squared projection residual without changing the solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq \frac{a}{2}\lVert x-p_a(x)\rVert^2\leq g_a(x)\leq g_{\mathrm{lin}}(x)\).

notation.meaning: Projection of x minus a^{-1}F(x) onto C.

knowledge_statements.title: D-Gap Merit Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference of two quadratically regularized VI gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(g_a\) using the penalty \(a\lVert x-y\rVert^2/2\). For parameters \(0<a<b\), the D-gap merit function is
\[
D_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x).
\]
Since increasing the penalty parameter decreases the regularized gap, \(D_{a,b}(x)\geq0\). In finite dimensions, the projection characterization of the two regularized gaps gives
\[
D_{a,b}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=P_C(x-a^{-1}F(x)),
\]
so the D-gap vanishes exactly at solutions of the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The D-gap subtracts a more strongly regularized gap from a less strongly regularized one, producing a nonnegative merit function with the VI solution set as its zeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{a,b}(x)=g_a(x)-g_b(x)\geq0\), and \(D_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).

notation.meaning: D-gap formed from regularization parameters a and b.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula and zero-set assertion are standard for this quadratic-penalty convention, and definition is the correct role, but no citation is supplied. A source must confirm the parameter ordering and exact D-gap convention.

children.title: Natural Residuals
children.top_down_role: Natural-map residual certificates for constrained variational inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point displacement residual for a projected VI step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and choose \(t>0\). The step-\(t\) natural residual is
\[
N_t(x):=x-P_C(x-tF(x)),\qquad x\in C.
\]
Its norm is a nonnegative, directly computable certificate. The projection optimality condition gives
\[
N_t(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Thus the natural residual vanishes exactly at solutions of the variational inequality, without requiring monotonicity of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual is the displacement generated by one projected operator step, and it is zero exactly at variational-inequality solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_t(x)=0\iff x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).

children.title: Projected Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates obtained through projection-based mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stepsize-normalized displacement of a projected VI update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(t>0\). The projected residual is
\[
R_t(x):=\frac{1}{t}\bigl(x-P_C(x-tF(x))\bigr),\qquad x\in C.
\]
The normalization gives \(R_t\) the same scale as the operator. Projection optimality yields
\[
R_t(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Hence either the vector \(R_t(x)\) or its norm provides an exact residual certificate for the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected residual is the projected-step displacement divided by the stepsize; it has operator scale and vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t(x)=t^{-1}[x-P_C(x-tF(x))]\), and \(R_t(x)=0\iff x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).

children.title: Natural–Projected Residual Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Geometric and scaling regimes governing comparability of the two residual forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural–Projected Residual Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scaling equivalence for a common projected VI step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a mapping \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(t>0\), define the natural and projected residuals using the same projection point \(P_C(x-tF(x))\). Then
\[
R_t(x)=t^{-1}N_t(x),
\qquad
\lVert R_t(x)\rVert=t^{-1}\lVert N_t(x)\rVert.
\]
Therefore the two residuals have identical zero sets and give equivalent error tests for fixed \(t\):
\[
\lVert N_t(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lVert R_t(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon/t.
\]
Their numerical magnitudes differ only by the chosen stepsize normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When based on the same projected step, natural and projected residuals differ only by the reciprocal stepsize and therefore have identical zeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t=t^{-1}N_t\), so \(R_t(x)=0\iff N_t(x)=0\iff x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).

children.title: Normal-Map Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates expressed through normal-map representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal-map residual for a constrained variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(P_C\) denote Euclidean projection onto \(C\). For \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\), set \(x=P_Cz\). The normal map and its residual are
\[
F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z):=F(x)+z-x,
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{nor}}(z):=\lVert F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)\rVert.
\]
Thus \(r_{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=0\) exactly when \(F(P_Cz)+z-P_Cz=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-map residual is the norm of the normal map obtained by projecting an unconstrained point onto the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=\lVert F(P_Cz)+z-P_Cz\rVert\), and it vanishes precisely at a zero of the normal map.

notation.meaning: normal map induced by F and C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and zero characterization are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no source with an inspectable normal-map locator is supplied.

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates expressed through fixed-point mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected fixed-point residual for a constrained variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(P_C:\mathbb{R}^d\to C\) denote Euclidean projection, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). For \(x\in C\), define
\[
T_\gamma(x):=P_C\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr),
\qquad
R_\gamma(x):=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-T_\gamma(x)\bigr),
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{fp},\gamma}(x):=\lVert R_\gamma(x)\rVert.
\]
Then \(r_{\mathrm{fp},\gamma}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=T_\gamma(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fixed-point residual is the scaled displacement between a feasible point and its projected forward step, and it vanishes exactly at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{fp},\gamma}(x)=0\iff x=P_C(x-\gamma F(x))\).

children.title: Normal-Map–Fixed-Point Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representation links and metric dependencies connecting the two residual families.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map–Fixed-Point Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-set correspondence for Euclidean projection and positive stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:C\to\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(\gamma>0\). Then
\[
0\in F(x)+N_C(x)
\iff x=P_C\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr).
\]
Moreover, if \(x\) satisfies these conditions and \(z=x-\gamma F(x)\), then \(P_Cz=x\) and the scaled normal map \(F(x)+\gamma^{-1}(z-x)\) vanishes. Conversely, any \(z\) with \(x=P_Cz\) and \(F(x)+\gamma^{-1}(z-x)=0\) yields the fixed-point equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solutions, projected fixed points, and zeros of the scaled normal map correspond through the change of variables z=x−γF(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution set of \(0\in F+N_C\) equals the fixed-point set, and is in bijection with the corresponding normal-map zeros.

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-cone stationarity residual for a constrained variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(x\in C\), and let \(F(x)\in\mathbb{R}^d\). With \(T_C(x)\) the tangent cone, define the tangent residual vector and magnitude by
\[
d_T(x):=P_{T_C(x)}\bigl(-F(x)\bigr),
\qquad
r_T(x):=\lVert d_T(x)\rVert.
\]
Because \(N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ\), one has \(r_T(x)=0\) exactly when \(-F(x)\in N_C(x)\), equivalently \(0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent residual is the norm of the feasible first-order component of −F(x); it vanishes exactly at variational-inequality stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_T(x)=0\iff 0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to C at x
Euclidean projection onto the tangent cone

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tangent-cone projection residual and its stationarity zero set are correct for a closed convex set, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Gradient-Mapping Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space gradient mapping for smooth constrained minimax problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(L:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable on an open set \(U\supseteq X\times Y\). For \(z=(x,y)\in X\times Y\), set \(F(z):=(\nabla_xL(x,y),-\nabla_yL(x,y))\). Given \(\gamma>0\), define
\[
G_\gamma(z):=\gamma^{-1}\left[z-P_{X\times Y}\bigl(z-\gamma F(z)\bigr)\right],
\qquad
r_\gamma(z):=\lVert G_\gamma(z)\rVert.
\]
Then \(r_\gamma(z)=0\) if and only if \(z=P_{X\times Y}(z-\gamma F(z))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimax gradient-mapping residual is the scaled displacement produced by projected descent in x and projected ascent in y, and it vanishes exactly at a projected fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(L:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable on an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\gamma(z)=0\iff z=P_{X\times Y}(z-\gamma F(z))\).

children.title: Ergodic Certificates
children.top_down_role: Averaged and weighted output certificates central to monotone VI complexity theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual gap certificate for averaged convex-concave iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty compact convex sets, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second. For iterates \((x_t,y_t)\) and weights \(\lambda_t\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{t=1}^T\lambda_t=1\), define \(\bar x_T=\sum_t\lambda_tx_t\) and \(\bar y_T=\sum_t\lambda_ty_t\). The ergodic certificate is
\[
\mathcal G_T:=\sup_{y\in Y}L(\bar x_T,y)-\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\bar y_T).
\]
A bound \(\mathcal G_T\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual gap of weighted average iterates certifies their saddle-point accuracy over compact comparison domains.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(L\) is convex-concave and real-valued on \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_T\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-saddle point at \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Accuracy Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted variational-inequality certificate controlling the gap at the averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(F:Z\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be monotone. Given \(z_t\in Z\) and weights \(\lambda_t\geq0\) with \(\sum_{t=1}^T\lambda_t=1\), define
\[
\bar z_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T\lambda_tz_t,
\qquad
\varepsilon_T:=\sup_{z\in Z}\sum_{t=1}^T\lambda_t\langle F(z_t),z_t-z\rangle.
\]
Then the dual gap at the average satisfies
\[
\sup_{z\in Z}\langle F(z),\bar z_T-z\rangle\leq\varepsilon_T.
\]
Hence \(\varepsilon_T\leq\varepsilon\) is a weighted accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum of iterate-wise variational inequalities upper-bounds the dual gap of the weighted average.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{z\in Z}\langle F(z),\bar z_T-z\rangle\leq\varepsilon_T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity-based weighted certificate inequality is mathematically correct and fits the leaf, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Ergodic Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-gap certificate for random ergodic saddle-point iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty compact convex sets, let \(L\) be convex-concave, and let \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\) be a random weighted average of feasible iterates. Define the random gap
\[
\mathcal G_T:=\sup_{y\in Y}L(\bar x_T,y)-\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\bar y_T).
\]
If an analysis based on conditionally unbiased stochastic first-order oracles establishes \(\mathbb E[\mathcal G_T]\leq\varepsilon\), then the averaged output is an expected \(\varepsilon\)-saddle point. If additionally \(\mathbb P\{\mathcal G_T\leq\varepsilon_\delta\}\geq1-\delta\), then \(\varepsilon_\delta\) is a confidence-level certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected or high-probability bounds on the random ergodic primal-dual gap certify stochastic saddle-point accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, compact, and convex, and \(L\) is convex-concave.
The stochastic oracle errors are conditionally mean zero relative to the iteration history.
The averaged iterates are measurable and feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\mathcal G_T]\leq\varepsilon\) gives expected accuracy; \(\mathbb P\{\mathcal G_T\leq\varepsilon_\delta\}\geq1-\delta\) gives confidence \(1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expected-gap and high-probability implications are valid as certificate statements, but no source specifies the stochastic oracle model, measurability conditions, or concentration framework.

children.title: Certificate Stopping-Validation Interface
children.top_down_role: Computable stopping routes and the boundary between certified and heuristic monitoring.

children.title: Gap-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Stopping interfaces driven by computable saddle, primal–dual, or VI gap values.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping rule based on a computable upper bound for a finite saddle-point gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\in X\times Y\). Assume the gap
\[
\mathcal G(z_k):=\sup_{y\in Y}L(x_k,y)-\inf_{x\in X}L(x,y_k)
\]
is finite, and suppose a computable quantity \(U_k\in[0,\infty)\) satisfies \(\mathcal G(z_k)\leq U_k\). For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), define
\[
\tau:=\inf\{k\geq0:U_k\leq\varepsilon\}.
\]
Whenever \(\tau<\infty\), the returned point satisfies \(\mathcal G(z_\tau)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a computable upper bound on the finite primal-dual gap reaches the requested tolerance; every finite stopping index then carries the corresponding gap guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\in X\times Y\) and \(\mathcal G(z_k)\) is finite.
\(U_k\) is computable and satisfies \(\mathcal G(z_k)\leq U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau<\infty\implies\mathcal G(z_\tau)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: computable upper bound on the gap

children.title: Residual-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Stopping interfaces driven by natural, projected, fixed-point, or related residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping rule using a residual with a valid error calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_k\geq0\) be a computable residual at iterate \(z_k\), and let \(E(z_k)\) denote the target error. Assume a known nondecreasing calibration function \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) satisfies \(E(z_k)\leq\phi(r_k)\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), stop at
\[
\tau:=\inf\{k\geq0:\phi(r_k)\leq\varepsilon\}.
\]
Then every finite stopping index certifies \(E(z_\tau)\leq\varepsilon\). Without the calibration inequality, a small residual alone need not certify the chosen target error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a calibrated residual upper bound reaches tolerance; residual size alone is insufficient without a valid error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau<\infty\implies E(z_\tau)\leq\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional stopping implication is correct, but the substantive residual-to-error calibration is problem-class dependent and has no supporting source or specified class.

children.title: Certificate Calibration
children.top_down_role: Scaling and threshold comparability across gap-based and residual-based monitors.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided calibration between certificate values and a target accuracy measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C(z)\geq0\) be a computable certificate and \(E(z)\geq0\) the target error on a domain \(D\). A two-sided calibration on \(D\) consists of nondecreasing functions \(\underline\phi,\overline\phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\), both vanishing at zero, such that
\[
\underline\phi(E(z))\leq C(z)\leq\overline\phi(E(z))
\qquad\text{for every }z\in D.
\]
For stopping validity, the essential direction is an error bound \(E(z)\leq\psi(C(z))\). Consequently, the threshold \(C(z)\leq\psi^{-1}_{\mathrm{safe}}(\varepsilon)\) certifies \(E(z)\leq\varepsilon\), where the safe inverse is chosen to preserve this implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calibration translates certificate values into target-error guarantees; the stopping threshold must use the implication-valid inverse direction.
assumptions_latex: The calibration functions are nondecreasing and vanish at zero.
A valid bound \(E(z)\leq\psi(C(z))\) is known on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certificate threshold is valid only when it implies the requested bound \(E(z)\leq\varepsilon\) throughout \(D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf is appropriate, but the safe inverse is not defined and the assumptions do not state the monotonicity or generalized-inverse condition needed to derive a threshold from E(z)≤ψ(C(z)). A sourced calibration convention is required before fixing the statement.

children.title: Restricted-Domain Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation using bounded or application-specific comparison domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Domain Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap validation against prescribed subsets of comparison points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X'\subseteq X\) and \(Y'\subseteq Y\) be nonempty comparison sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second, and let \((\hat x,\hat y)\in X\times Y\). Define
\[
\mathcal G_{X',Y'}(\hat x,\hat y):=\sup_{y\in Y'}L(\hat x,y)-\inf_{x\in X'}L(x,\hat y).
\]
The inequality \(\mathcal G_{X',Y'}(\hat x,\hat y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies the saddle inequalities only against deviations in \(X'\times Y'\). It also certifies the full-domain gap when
\[
\sup_{y\in Y'}L(\hat x,y)=\sup_{y\in Y}L(\hat x,y)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\inf_{x\in X'}L(x,\hat y)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\hat y).
\]
Containment in \(Y'\) and \(X'\) of full-domain maximizers and minimizers, when they exist, is a sufficient condition for these equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted gap validates deviations only over the selected comparison sets. It is also a full-domain certificate when the restricted and full extremal values agree; containment of full-domain extremizers is one sufficient way to ensure this.
assumptions_latex: \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_{X',Y'}(\hat x,\hat y)\leq\varepsilon\) is a restricted-domain certificate and becomes a full-domain certificate when the stated extremal-value equalities hold.

children.title: Statistical Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation using sampled evaluations, confidence controls, or held-out operator information.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-deviation validation of an empirical saddle-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be a population saddle function, and let \(\widehat L\) be its empirical counterpart. Define \(G_L(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y)\), and define \(G_{\widehat L}\) analogously. On any event satisfying \(\sup_{(u,v)\in X\times Y}|L(u,v)-\widehat L(u,v)|\leq\delta\), every reported pair \((\widehat x,\widehat y)\) with \(G_{\widehat L}(\widehat x,\widehat y)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) satisfies \[G_L(\widehat x,\widehat y)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}+2\delta.\] Thus the empirical gap and a simultaneous deviation bound form a verifiable population-level certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empirical saddle gap plus twice a uniform estimation error bounds the population saddle gap on the same validation event.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, and all displayed suprema and infima are finite.
\(\sup_{X\times Y}|L-\widehat L|\leq\delta\) holds on the stated validation event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_L(\widehat x,\widehat y)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}+2\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic uniform-deviation transfer for saddle gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-deviation transfer is mathematically precise, the plain and LaTeX statements agree, and certificate is the correct content kind for this validation leaf. However, source_refs is empty, so the population-level certificate lacks the required inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Domain-to-Statistical Validation Links
children.top_down_role: Interactions between comparison-domain choice and statistical reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-to-Statistical Validation Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of full-domain population error into restricted empirical, statistical, and domain-approximation terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_R\subseteq X\) and \(Y_R\subseteq Y\) be nonempty validation domains. For \((x,y)\in X_R\times Y_R\), define the restricted gap \(G_R^L(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y_R}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X_R}L(u,y)\) and the domain bias \[b_R^L(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\sup_{v\in Y_R}L(x,v)+\inf_{u\in X_R}L(u,y)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y).\] Then \(G_L(x,y)=G_R^L(x,y)+b_R^L(x,y)\). If \(\sup_{X_R\times Y_R}|L-\widehat L|\leq\delta_R\), then \[G_L(x,y)\leq G_R^{\widehat L}(x,y)+2\delta_R+b_R^L(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full population gap equals a restricted-domain gap plus domain bias; uniform statistical deviation adds at most twice its size.
assumptions_latex: All suprema and infima defining the gaps and bias are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_L(x,y)\leq G_R^{\widehat L}(x,y)+2\delta_R+b_R^L(x,y)\).

notation.meaning: Population saddle gap restricted to the validation domains.
Loss from replacing the full domains by restricted domains.
Uniform empirical deviation on the restricted product domain.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic gap decomposition and uniform-deviation transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact gap decomposition and the two-delta restricted-domain transfer are internally consistent, and representation correctly describes this domain-to-statistical link. No inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Ergodic Convergence Families
